| statistics core record | O(n) counts, sums and histograms (the expensive metrics run on demand or in the bench; SCL-21) | — | 4 ms |
| model digest | per-batch digests maintained inside each stage (SCL-1); finalisation | — | 5 ms |
| **critical path** | | | **≈ 255 ms p50; p95 ≤ 300 ms** |
| S14 city band (outside the model budget; counted in the first frame) | columnar build for every district | ≈ 60 000 marks | 20 ms |

Stated assumptions: stage rates include stream-key derivation at ≤ 0.1 µs per key (§6.1; the rows were costed at 0.3 µs,
SCL-12), model-digest maintenance ≤ 5 % of each batch's time with finalisation ≤ 5 ms and a full recompute ≤ 150 ms at
CITY (§6.2), and no whole-level static index rebuild per commit (SCL-2). There is one geometry engine on every host
(§3.7): S9 and S11 are budgeted once, for it, and the generation report names the engine that ran (SCL-22); the earlier
"pure-JS boolean fallback at 2.5×" assumption is withdrawn with the fallback itself (integration record C-8). The
single-worker CITY path is ≈ 334 ms p50 (the pooled 48 ms becomes 116 ms, the hinterland unit's ≈ 15 ms joins the
critical path, and no arena copies are made). METROPOLIS: raster and lattice work × ≈ 2.6 (frame area), entity work ×
2.5 — ≈ 609 ms p50 with the pool (copies ≈ 37 MB, ≈ 3.9 ms each, measured), ≈ 801 ms single-worker. TOWN: ≈ 76 ms p50
with the pool. (Round 1's integration added the S7b row and the single travel-cost field, +6 ms at CITY; round 2 moved
the gate routes and the stage-1 field into S3 (net 0), added S12a's siting, the eager shared-edge step and the pool's
arena copies (+6 ms at CITY); round 3 added step (0)'s L3 partition rebuild before the freeze (+2.3 ms at CITY, +5.8 ms
at METROPOLIS, ≈ +1 ms at TOWN; VK2-1); round 4 counted the static index partitions in the pool's copies (+2 ms at CITY,
+3 ms at METROPOLIS; TOWN's partitions add ≈ 0.3 ms; the single-worker path makes no copies; VK3-6); all PLAUSIBLE until
the fusion gate and the M0 site-and-fields spike measure them. The p95 laws of §12.3 are unchanged.)

**M0 site-and-fields spike** (beside the fusion gate, which covers S4 + S5 + S8): S1 + S4 + S6 ≤ 50 ms at CITY with these
mechanisms, starting from redteam-scale §7's scripts. Pre-decided fallback: raster cells coarsen one step (fields and the
margin 32 → 48 m; hydrology 25 → 32 m at CITY, METROPOLIS 32 → 40 m, TOWN 16 → 20 m) and the spike re-runs.

### 12.5 First map, frames, zoom, pan, draw calls, uploads (SCL-7, SCL-17, VIS-6)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r2); drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r2

**The first map is a law of the building count (N-2).** Size follows population inside a rung (§1.1), so the first-map
budget is a function of B, the number of buildings the request generates (≈ population ÷ 3.4, §12.2), never one number
per rung. Time to first map — click → the complete city band on screen, Canvas2D `ink`, the reference viewport — is
§12.3's model law plus the **first-frame law**

  F(B) ≤ 20 ms + 10 µs × B

made of S14's city band (≈ 4 µs per building, §12.4), the delivery of the column slices to the tile worker (≈ 1 µs),
the city-band raster (≈ 5 µs per building plus 0.25 ms per tile position), S13b at the first stop (≤ 2 ms), the label
composition (≈ 0.1 ms per position plus ≈ 1 µs per glyph) and the commit of the composed tiles (≈ 0.1 ms per position),
for the **reference viewport** — 1 440 × 900 CSS px at device pixel ratio 2, whose worst tile alignment covers P = 35
positions of 512² device px (§8.8), so the fixed terms sum to ≈ 19 ms. Laws and values
(`docs/validation/bench/fixall_rendering_r2_budgets.out`):

| rung | buildings B, band bottom → top | time to first map T(B), pool | T at the band's bottom / the default request / the top | the rung's bar holds up to | single-worker fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TOWN | 440 → 2 940 | ≤ 40 ms + 70 µs × B | 71 ms / 124–145 ms / 246 ms | 150 ms: B ≤ 1 570 (≈ 5 300 people) | ≤ 40 ms + 81 µs × B (138–162 ms at the default) |
| CITY | 2 940 → 8 820 | ≤ 60 ms + 60 µs × B | 236 ms / 330–420 ms / 589 ms | 0.4 s: B ≤ 5 670 (≈ 19 300 people) | ≤ 60 ms + 79 µs × B (416–535 ms) |
| METROPOLIS | 8 820 → 35 000 | ≤ 120 ms + 62 µs × B | 667 ms / 864–1 050 ms / 2 290 ms | 1 s: B ≤ 14 190 (≈ 48 000 people) | ≤ 120 ms + 77 µs × B (1.04–1.27 s; 1 s up to B ≈ 11 400) |

"The default request" is each rung's target population, whose building count §12.2 gives as a range (1 200–1 500,
4 500–6 000, 12 000–15 000); the bottom and top are the band's population ends at 3.4 persons per building.

**Where O12 (g)'s one second holds, and the declared miss.** The first map is under one second for every TOWN and
every CITY request (their band tops are 246 ms and 589 ms) and for METROPOLIS up to ≈ 14 200 buildings (≈ 48 000
people); the default METROPOLIS request (50 000 people) lands at 0.86–1.05 s across its building range. Above
≈ 14 200 buildings the first map grows by 62 µs per building, to ≈ 2.3 s at the 35 000-building cap (120 000 people).
**Declared for the owner's veto:** chose to keep the one-click path complete at every size — every plot, site plan and
building at city-band detail, no preview (J-R7, J-I2) — over holding one second above the knee, because the model's
cost is linear in buildings (§12.3), and the only ways under the bar there are a partial picture, whose figure-ground
differs from the finished map (MFP-1), or dropping plot and site-plan detail from the one-click path, which the
owner's plot-model ruling forbids. Reversing costs ≈ 1 person-week: above the knee, the city band would appear district
by district as the pool finishes them, with the labels last. With the single-worker fallback the knee is ≈ 11 400
buildings (≈ 39 000 people).

**Measurement and fallback (N-2, N-27 c).** B-CITY's browser runs time the first map at each band's bottom, default
request and top — TOWN at 1 500 / 5 000 / 9 900 people and CITY at 10 000 / 20 000 / 29 900 at M1, METROPOLIS at
30 000 / 50 000 / 120 000 at M2b — five seeds each on the reference machine, and fit both terms of each law. Pass:
every p95 within its law + 10 %. Pre-decided fallbacks: a raster-side miss (the measured first frame above F(B))
steps the tier's tile DPR down one level for every view (2 → 1.5; P falls from 35 to 24, cutting the per-position
terms by a third), fixed at the milestone and reported, and the run repeats; a model-side miss is §12.3's (the
single-worker column, or the model law re-declared at the measured p95 as a D-18 amendment for the owner's veto),
after which this table is re-derived from the measured laws and the knee re-stated to the owner.

**Interaction** at 40 000 buildings and 200 000 trees (O12 b): **pan** ≥ 60 fps on the reference machine and ≥ 30 fps
on the low-end device (compositing cached tiles; ≤ 4 ms of main-thread work per frame); **zoom gestures** at the same
rates (scaled cached tiles); **settle**: the visible tiles re-rastered at the new stop within ≤ 150 ms for a CITY view
and ≤ 250 ms for a METROPOLIS view, centre-out, in the tile worker — assuming P ≤ 35 positions, the city band at
0.25 ms per position + 5 µs per visible building, the district band at 0.25 ms per position + 12 µs per visible
building, and 0.2 ms per position to compose and commit (a whole-CITY city-band view ≈ 42 ms, a whole-METROPOLIS view
≈ 83 ms, a district-band view of 3 000 buildings ≈ 52 ms); hairline fidelity at every settled view (§8.3).
**Confirmation (N-27 c):** settle and re-raster are measured with the first map (M1 on the reference and low-end
devices at TOWN and CITY, M2b at METROPOLIS), with the same pre-decided fallback (one tile-DPR step down on the tier
that missed); pan and zoom rates have §8.9's WebGL2 compositor as theirs.

**Draw calls:** ≤ 80 Canvas2D path fill and stroke calls per tile whatever the building count (batched per program and
semantic), so ≤ 80 × P per view (≤ 2 800 at the reference viewport), plus one sprite draw per visible crown and per
placed glyph (from the atlas). **Uploads (N-5):** while a pan or zoom gesture runs, ≤ 4 new composed bitmaps are
committed per animation frame, centre-out (baselines: NG 528 uploads per hood, MFCG 590 per city); at first paint and
at settle every ready tile is committed in the frame it arrives — one composed bitmap per position (§8.8), so a first
frame commits ≤ P bitmaps, not 2P, and no cap stretches it over frames; roof computations per frame after warm-up = 0
(derived roofs cached, §8.1). **Re-raster** at the district band ≤ 12 ms per 1 000 buildings (MFCG's replay costs
11–15 ms per 1 000). **Neighbourhood band:** opening one district ≤ NG's 10–96 ms at comparable counts; ≈ 25 canvas
operations per wing as the `hatched` ceiling.

No rung depends on WebGL2 (§8.9). Chose laws of the building count over one bar per rung because a single number held
only at each rung's target population while the ladder builds every population in the band (N-2).

### 12.6 Edits, regeneration, replay and warp, as functions of scope (SCL-9)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r5; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r2, drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r2

* **Scoped regeneration:** ≤ 3 ms + 60 µs × the buildings in scope (a district of ≤ 450 buildings in ≤ 30 ms), plus the
  S13a and S14 deltas ≤ 3 ms; the dirty tiles re-raster in the tile worker off the edit path (≤ 12 ms per 1 000
  buildings); edit-to-redraw < 100 ms.
* **A single plot edit:** ≤ 5 ms of model work plus ≤ 2 ms of deltas.
* **Coarse edits** (PLAUSIBLE; measured with §13.2's B-EDIT coarse-edit sequences): a course-knot, moved-shore or drawn-water
  edit ≤ 60 ms of model work at CITY for a re-traced reach ≤ 500 m (re-trace and carve ≈ 5 ms, crossing search ≈ 1 ms,
  the L1 batch of kept-way routes, deck vertices and cuts ≈ 5 ms,
  S4 re-route of ≤ 3 arterials ≈ 5 ms, S5 regrowth in ≤ 4 cells, F-REDERIVE of the touched blocks at the
  scoped-regeneration law); a terrain stroke ≤ 3 ms + 1 µs per re-based entity + the field-brush law for the blocks its
  drivers re-derive.
* **Scope invariance:** the same scope costs the same at TOWN, CITY and METROPOLIS within ± 20 % (a B-EDIT test:
  TOWN → CITY from M2a, TOWN → METROPOLIS from M2b, §13.2; NF-S6).
* **Replay and load verification (N-16, N-1).** Replay (load verification, migration, undo beyond the scoped records,
  the undo of an upgrade after a reload) folds the log on the model through the session's code path — S13a's scoped
  delta runs at each event that re-derives names, ≤ 3 ms per such event — and only S14 and S13b are suppressed and run
  once at the end (§7.3). Its cost is therefore a sum over the log, not a constant:

  V = M(B) + Σ c(e) + S14(B) + 5 ms

  where M(B) is §12.3's model law for the document's size (the recipe is replayed from S0; checkpoints are session
  memory, §7.4, and are not saved), S14(B) ≈ 4 µs × B is one display-list build, 5 ms finalises the model and records
  digests, and c(e) is
  each event's replay cost — its model scope cost, plus succession matching (≤ 2 µs per re-derived entity, §6.3), plus
  S13a's delta when it re-derives names: ≤ 0.5 ms for an event that re-derives nothing (attribute, label, lock, pin,
  style and table-row edits whose slices no entity reads); ≤ 8 ms for a plot-scale edit; ≤ 3 ms + 60 µs × the buildings
  in scope + matching + 3 ms for a scoped regeneration, a local operator (§7.3) or an epoch; ≤ M(B) for a Re-derive from
  Sk. For the **reference verification mix** of 300 edits on a CITY document of 5 200 buildings — 200 light edits, 80
  plot-scale edits, 15 block regenerations of ≤ 60 buildings and 5 district regenerations of ≤ 450 buildings — V ≈ 1.4 s
  p95 (`docs/validation/bench/fixall_rendering_r2_budgets.out`); a log of 300 district regenerations takes ≈ 11 s. The
  law replaces the earlier "300 edits in ≤ 1 s", which assumed checkpoints a saved document does not have. Verification
  never delays the picture or an edit: the saved model is displayed at once, editable once its own digest is recomputed
  and checked (§2.9 step 3; open-to-editable ≤ T(B), §12.5's law for the document's building count; the recomputation
  of its model and records trees ≈ 35–38 ms at CITY, measured synthetic (`fixall_det_r4_loaddigest.out`,
  `fixall_det_r5_recordsdigest.out`)), and verified by a replay in a pool worker beside the edits, while every edit
  made meanwhile runs its per-district stages single-worker in the generation worker (§2.9 step 3); with pool size 0
  the replay itself runs in the generation worker and yields to each edit at its next batch boundary (§2.9 steps 3–4);
  the report shows the law's estimate and the progress, and "trust the saved town" ends the wait once the saved copy's
  own roots have matched (NR-8, VD4-2). B-EDIT times the reference mix at M2a (pass: ≤ V + 10 %); pre-decided fallback: the
  per-kind costs c(e) are re-declared at their measured p95 and the reference mix's V restated here, reported for the
  owner's veto (the verification wait is off the path to the picture, so no mechanism changes). Chose to state the bound
  as a law of the log over saving checkpoints because a checkpoint holds the arena chunks changed since the last one,
  which would multiply the 3 MB CITY document (§2.9) for edit-heavy files, while the verification wait is already off
  the path to the picture.
* **Warp preview:** ≥ 30 fps for a brush radius ≤ 150 m; Apply ≤ the scoped-regeneration budget of the touched faces,
  counting §2.6's wing carry and check inside the whole-step validation — ≈ 0.4 ms per validation pass for 450
  buildings on an assumed core mix and ≈ 3.6 ms in the worst case of a step and eight halvings
  (`docs/validation/bench/fixall_pipeline_r5_wingcost.out`; §2.6 rule 4; NP4-6). *Measurement (M3a):* the Apply time
  of a 150 m brush over a CITY core on B-CITY-lite seeds, the carry and check counted. *Pre-decided fallback* if it
  exceeds the budget: the wing check leaves the whole-step validation — it runs once after the final step, and a
  building that fails it is re-derived by S11 on its plot (F-REDERIVE, reported) instead of halving the step (§2.6
  rule 4).
* **Proxy thumbnails:** §7.8's budget.

### 12.7 Labels, trees, exports (SCL-8, SCL-10, SCL-14)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r5; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3, drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r3

* **Labels:** S13a 12 ms at CITY and ≤ 30 ms at METROPOLIS (model); S13b ≤ 2 ms per zoom stop for ≤ 2 000 visible
  candidates — ≈ 1 µs per candidate, the rate an export's placement is budgeted at too (below) — run in resumable
  steps of one decision (§8.9, §9.2; NR4-2); a tile's label composition ≤ 3 ms at ≤ 150 glyph runs (§8.9).
* **Trees:** placement ≤ 1 µs and drawing ≤ 2 µs per instance. A district-band view with 10 000 visible trees composes in
  one 16 ms frame from cached tiles, and its tiles raster in ≤ 30 ms of tile-worker time (O19 e, restated); the 200 000
  trees of a METROPOLIS are never all instantiated — only visible tiles generate instances. The stamp-tile asset (§8.10)
  is loaded and hash-checked at worker start in ≤ 5 ms per worker per session (≈ 0.03–0.06 ms for 8–16 classes,
  measured cost model, `docs/validation/bench/fixall_rendering_r4_stamptiles.out`); nothing is sampled or ranked at run
  time, so the first zoom to the district band carries no library build (NR3-7). **The crown library (NR4-5):** its
  build (20 crowns per class per style, once per session) and, in `lit` with a `path` sun, each light step's bake run
  in the tile worker as one-sprite class-3 units (§8.9), ≤ 20 ms of tile-worker time per (style, light step) for eight
  crown classes (PLAUSIBLE: ≈ 20–60 µs per sprite on Canvas2D, ≈ 3–10 ms for 160 sprites), started when the style loads
  so the first district-band raster finds it ready; a light step's bake runs at the head of §8.4's light pass, inside
  its settle bound. Measured with M2b's moving-sun runs (§8.4), where `lit` ships; pre-decided fallback: §8.4's — with a
  `path` sun the lit programs and the crowns hold the sheet's fixed sun, so the library is baked once, reported.
* **SVG** at METROPOLIS, city band: ≤ 650 B per building plus the text — outlines ≤ 64 B per placed glyph and ≤ 0.5 KB
  per distinct glyph, or each embedded face's base64 bytes once (≤ 0.5 MB per face) (§11.1, N-13) — and ≤ 60 000
  elements, written in ≤ 2 s in the generation worker — the transient list's build (≈ 4 µs per building, ≈ 54 ms at the
  METROPOLIS target), S13b at the export stop (≤ 2 ms per 2 000 candidates) and the writing, with the list released
  after it (§11.1; NR-5); Inkscape opens it within 120 s (§11.1).
* **PNG:** A2 at 300 dpi of a CITY in ≤ 20 s on the reference machine **with the view idle**, the peak canvas one tile
  band. Inside it: the transient list's build in the generation worker (≈ 4 µs per building at the city band —
  ≈ 21 ms at CITY — and more at the finer band a large print's scale selects; §8.7, §11.1); the export's placement in
  the tile worker (≈ 1 µs per candidate in the frame — ≤ 20 ms for 20 000 candidates, more than a whole CITY's label
  rows at any band: ≈ 3 500 names, §12.4, one address per building and the repeats of long street names — in class-4
  steps, §8.9; NR4-2); and the
  encoding (§8.8's per-row filter rule, then the deflate), measured on a synthetic A2 map in Node 24
  (`docs/validation/bench/fixall_rendering_r5_png.out`) at 3.5 s for flat `ink`-like colours, 5.4 s under smooth
  relief shading and 10.5 s for a textured `lit`-like look, of which the filter pass takes 2.7 to 3.4 s and the
  deflate the rest
  (PLAUSIBLE for browsers, whose filter pass is the same JavaScript and whose deflate is native code behind
  `CompressionStream`). View
  work pre-empts the export's steps (§8.9), so a pan or zoom during an export lengthens it by that work, which the
  export dialog's progress shows, and an animated view still leaves it one step in every 100 ms (NR3-6).
* **Confirmation of the export budgets (N-27 c).** The SVG and PNG budgets are measured at M1 on B-CITY-lite's TOWN and
  CITY seeds and at M2b on METROPOLIS. Pre-decided fallbacks, taken once and reported: an SVG size or element miss at
  the city band writes path coordinates with one decimal of the export's unit instead of two and merges compound paths
  per (semantic, quarter of the city cut) instead of per (semantic, district), re-keying the `<metadata>` map; a
  district-band SVG that misses its estimate draws woods and orchards as their outlines instead of crowns; a PNG time
  miss is answered per host, the same pixels in a larger file each time (NR4-4): **on every host** the row filter is
  fixed to type None for every row instead of §8.8's per-row rule — on the synthetic A2 the filter pass disappears and
  the unfiltered rows also deflate faster, so encoding falls from 3.5, 5.4 and 10.5 s to 0.6, 1.3 and 4.4 s for the
  flat, relief and textured looks, the file 4 % smaller to 10 % larger; **in Node**, whose `zlib` takes a level, a miss that
  remains deflates at level 3 instead of 6 (a further 0.35–2.5 s on the synthetic looks, the file 8–51 % larger);
  **in browsers**, whose `CompressionStream` takes a format and no options — in Node 24's implementation of the same
  standard a `{ level }` option is ignored, 5.3 MiB with none, level 1 and level 9 alike — a miss that remains after
  the filter change re-declares the PNG budget at the measured p95 as a D-18 amendment for the owner's veto. Chose type
  None over the fixed Sub filter as the fallback because, measured on all three looks, None is both faster and no
  larger — Sub still spends ≈ 0.2 s filtering and deflates as slowly as the default, and its files are 7–30 % larger
  than the default's — and chose §8.8's per-row rule as the default over None because it gives the smallest file
  wherever rows carry gradients or texture (7–10 % smaller on the relief and textured looks) and the budget has room
  for its filter pass. **Export beside the view
  (NR3-6):** B-CITY's browser run at M1 adds a scripted pan and zoom during an A2 300-dpi export of a CITY, in §12.1's
  timing phase — pass: every settle within §12.5's bound, the export completes, and its PNG matches, byte for byte, the
  export made with the view idle and one during which an edit is made (§8.9, §11.1); pre-decided fallback:
  §8.9's `step(4)`. **The stamp-tile load (NR3-7)** is timed with the first map at M1, per worker from worker start to
  the library ready; pre-decided fallback on a miss: the per-session hash check moves to CI and the release build,
  leaving typed-array views over the bundled bytes.
* **Stage-3 hook (§2.6; SCL-13):** the base outline builder's `outline()` is inside S11's geometry share (≤ 3 µs per plot
  median, §3.7); a stage-3 generator's `outline()` is admitted at ≤ 10 µs per building median and its registration
  re-declares S11's row of §12.4 by the measured difference (§2.6, §3.7); `compose()` ≤ 1 ms per building median at
  `wings`, in the derivation pool on the tile's band request (§8.6, §8.9), one tile's
  compositions within 16 ms of pool time, amortised (a tile draws the outline until its compositions arrive).
* **Simulation module (§10.3; FTG-11):** one hour of occupancy for 50 000 people ≤ 50 ms in the worker, with a cost-model
  test (§13.2); never on the one-click path.

### 12.8 Memory (what is counted, per rung)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3, drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r3

Counted: the JS heap, typed arrays and WebAssembly memory of every thread (generation worker, pool, tile worker, main),
with canvas backing stores budgeted separately.

| rung | model working set, all threads, excluding canvases | canvas budget: need at the reference viewport; tier ceilings low / mid / high |
|---|---|---|
| TOWN | ≤ 40 MB | 3P + 7 MB = 112 MB at P = 35; 72 / 128 / 192 MB |
| CITY | ≤ 110 MB | the same (the canvas need depends on the viewport, not the rung) |
| METROPOLIS | ≤ 260 MB | the same |

**The tile worker holds no model (N-4).** It holds the display list — the only full copy, ≈ 10 MB at CITY with its
label, instance and string tables (§8.1 item 6) — the decoration memo and the placement memo; its glyph atlases and
crown sprites are canvases, counted in the canvas budget. The generation worker holds the model and keeps a
24-B-per-mark index of the display list (≈ 1.4 MB at CITY); the derivation pool holds its per-worker overlays (§4.1) and
the on-demand `compose()` and close-up caches (§8.6). These lines assume one kernel arena per layer (≈ 20 MB at CITY
with its typed lookup tables, its spatial index and the index's home column, §2.2; PLAUSIBLE until M1) plus one frozen
arena copy per pool worker (≤ ≈ 15 MB each at CITY at the one-click freeze, ≈ 20 MB at a freeze after edits; ≈ 37 MB at
METROPOLIS; VK3-6) and each district overlay until it merges (§3.3), the compact entity store and the scoped undo
records of §2 and §7.4 (SCL-5), people derived on demand, tree instances never stored, and the display list at ≈ 11.4 MB
at CITY across the two threads that hold any of it. The earlier "≈ 6 MB per thread that holds it" undercounted the fixed
columns — 46 B per mark, now 54 B with the render key (N-9 c; §8.1 item 5) — and assumed a full copy in both the
generation worker and the tile worker (≈ 12 MB); keeping one full copy brings the corrected display list back under that
figure. The pool's frozen arena copies (≈ 45 MB at CITY with three workers at the one-click freeze, ≈ 60 MB at a freeze
after edits; `Map`-based tables would have cost each worker more heap and ≈ 10–20 ms of rebuild, VK2-9) are new in round
2 (§3.3); while a loaded document is verified, one pool worker holds the replay's model in their place — no frozen copy
is made while verification runs, because every edit made meanwhile runs its per-district stages in the generation worker
by the pool-size-0 path (§2.9 step 3; VD3-5), and the replay's arena and entity columns are about the copies' size — or,
with pool size 0, the generation worker holds it beside the working state (§2.9 step 3; NR-8), and M2a's memory
measurement below — the milestone that builds the log and load verification over the document format M1 builds (§16;
VS4-3) — includes the load verification of the reference 300-edit CITY document with a district regeneration and a
Re-derive from S3 made during it; the load's digest trees (the model tree ≈ 1 MB and the records tree ≈ 0.25 MB at CITY,
§6.2) sit in the entity-store line, and a bridged client that took the replayed town keeps the `doc.load` bytes (≤ 3 MB
at CITY) until the mismatch is settled (§2.9 step 4); the lines are kept and stay PLAUSIBLE until M1 (generated towns at
TOWN and CITY), M2a (that load-verification case at CITY) and M2b (METROPOLIS) measure them, with the steps below as
their pre-decided fallbacks.

**The CITY line, itemised (≤ 110 MB; VK3-6).** At the one-click freeze the fixed items are the arena (≈ 20 MB), three
frozen copies (≈ 45 MB) and the display list (≈ 11.4 MB across the tile worker's copy and the generation worker's index)
— ≈ 76 MB — leaving ≈ 34 MB for the **entity-store line** — the compact entity store with the load's digest trees (≈
1.25 MB) and, on a bridged client during a load mismatch, the kept `doc.load` bytes (≤ 3 MB) — and for the terrain,
hydrology and field rasters, the district overlays until they merge, the scoped undo records, the decoration and
placement memos and each thread's runtime baseline. At a freeze after edits the copies are ≈ 60 MB and the fixed items ≈
91 MB, leaving ≈ 19 MB; that case has its own first fallback step below. All PLAUSIBLE until M1 measures them.

**Export-time peak (NR-5, NR3-6).** An export that draws holds a transient display list while it runs (§11.1) — SVG
in the generation worker while it writes; PNG, print and the `.dd2vtt` image in the tile worker, to which the list is
transferred with the request, until the last band is encoded (§8.9): ≈ 1.9 KB per building at the city band (§8.1 item 6's ≈ 10 MB for ≈ 5 200 buildings) — ≈ 2.6 MB at the TOWN
target, ≈ 10 MB at CITY, ≈ 26 MB at the METROPOLIS target and ≈ 67 MB at the 35 000-building cap
(`docs/validation/bench/fixall_rendering_r3_budgets.out`) — plus the file being written (≤ 650 B per building for SVG at
the city band, §12.7; a PNG's streamed bytes), both released when the file is transferred out. It is counted on top of
each rung's line as a peak, not in the steady working set, and one export runs at a time. A district-band export's
list — a district-band SVG, or a large print whose scale selects the district band (§8.7) — enters the size estimate
the export dialog shows before it starts; its size per band is measured with the export budgets below. A raster export
also holds canvases: one band (width × 512 × 4 B, ≈ 14 MB at A2 300 dpi, §8.8) and the canvas of the tile job in
progress (1 MB), counted with the canvases below. Measured
with the export budgets (M1 TOWN and CITY, M2b METROPOLIS, §12.7) — pass: within the stated figure + 25 %.
Pre-decided fallback: the transient list is built with only the attribute columns the sheet's programs read at the
export band, for every export that draws, (the attribute columns are up to ≈ 2.4 of the ≈ 10 MB at CITY, §8.1 item 6), the figure is re-stated at
the new measurement, and the export dialog's size estimate uses it.

**Canvas budget (N-9 b).** The need is 3P + 7 MB (4.25P + 7 MB with path-mode shadow layers), P being the worst-case
tile positions of the viewport at the tile DPR; each tier has a ceiling, and the tile DPR steps down until the need
fits it (§8.8). The reference view (1 440 × 900 at DPR 2) needs 112 MB; the low-end device's 1 366 × 768 or
1 920 × 1 080 at DPR 1 needs 43 or 67 MB. **During a raster export (NR3-6)** its ≈ 15 MB of canvases count on top of the
view's need: the reference view on the mid tier (112 + 15 ≤ 128 MB) and the low-end 1 366 × 768 view (43 + 15 ≤ 72 MB)
hold both; where the sum passes the tier's ceiling — the low tier at 1 920 × 1 080 (67 + 15 > 72 MB) — the coarser-stop
fallback set is dropped for the export's duration (the need falls to 2P + 7 MB: 47 + 15 = 62 MB), and the export
dialog refuses a width whose band does not fit beside the reduced need, naming the widest that does.

**Measurement and fallback.** Measured per rung in B-CITY's browser runs at M1 (TOWN, CITY) and M2b (METROPOLIS), and at
M2a on the reference 300-edit CITY document under load verification (§16). Pre-decided fallback if CITY exceeds its line
at M1 or M2a: the provenance and lifecycle-history columns leave the working set for the document's on-demand block
(SCL-20's archive) and are decoded only when inspected; if the line is still exceeded at a freeze after edits, that
freeze makes the laziness-contract copy of §3.3 step 1 — L0–L2, every L3 partition, and only the L4 partitions of the
districts the pool derives (VK3-6); if the line is still exceeded, the pool shrinks by one worker per step (identical
digests by construction, §3.3) and the memory test re-runs. If a tier's canvases exceed its ceiling in the scripted pan
and zoom runs, its coarser-stop fallback set is dropped (the need falls to 2P + 7 MB) and a gesture shows the next
coarser cached tiles only where they remain. The document's size budget is §2.9's.

### 12.9 Reference comparisons and the declared trade

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r4); drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3, drafted by fixall/draft-rendering-r3

* **MFCG at matched building counts** (§12.2): model time 1.8× (TOWN), 2.3× (CITY) and 5.1× (METROPOLIS) MFCG's
  generation; time to first map, by §12.5's laws at MFCG's counts, ≈ 2× MFCG's generation plus canvas replay at TOWN
  and CITY (143 ms against 73–79 ms at 1 475 buildings; 374 ms against 189–210 ms at 5 242; MFCG's replay ≈ 11–15 µs per
  building, from its size-80 profile) and ≈ 3× at METROPOLIS (932 ms against 300–352 ms at 13 091); at MFCG's size-200
  stress count (31 951 buildings, 236 ms plus replay) PLAT's law gives ≈ 2.1 s, ≈ 3–3.6×.
* **FTG (NF-S7).** The side-by-side sizes are FTG's BIG_TOWN and BIG_CITY, from M-1's free captures (§13.6, D-31), and
  METROPOLIS per D-31. The timed capture so far is FTG's CITY preset (9 500 people, 2 798 buildings): the server answers
  in 2.9–3.2 s, the client is building the scene 6.4–7.0 s after the click, and loading a finished settlement costs 2.0 s
  of busy time (ftg-payload-visual, Critic-2 addendum part 2; the 4.6 s "client busy during create" figure is not a time
  to first map). PLAT's first map at that size (the TOWN law at 2 798 buildings) is ≈ 0.24 s, ≈ 27–30× sooner; FTG's
  creator gives ≈ 10 s to render a metropolis (49 500 people) client-side, ≈ 10× PLAT's ≈ 1.0 s at that population.
  M-1's BIG_TOWN and BIG_CITY captures add their timings to §13.5's timing row.
* **Declared trade (MFP-5, N-2, NR-1).** Chose a per-building cost of ≈ 58–75 µs at p95 (§12.3's laws at 1 333, 5 200
  and 13 460 buildings; NR3-5) over matching MFCG's 12–39 µs because PLAT builds what MFCG does not — a heightfield with
  hydrology, frontage-first plots with yards and party walls, site plans with heights, roster siting, greenery by rule
  and collision-checked labels — which D-7 ranks above speed. The first map stays under one second for every TOWN and
  CITY request and for METROPOLIS up to ≈ 14 200 buildings (≈ 48 000 people); above that it grows to ≈ 2.3 s at the 120
  000 cap, a miss of O12 (g) declared in §12.5 for the owner's veto. The model alone meets O3 (d)'s bars at p95 up to ≈
  4 500, 17 700 and 58 800 people and for the max up to ≈ 3 400, 13 600 and 45 800, and is slower above them — up to ≈
  0.2 s, 0.48 s and 1.9 s at the band tops — a miss declared in §12.3 for the owner's veto. Reversing the trade would
  mean dropping plot and site-plan detail from the one-click path, which the owner's plot-model ruling forbids.
* Chose the derivation pool as the primary configuration over a single worker because after LC-2's eager allocation the
  per-district stages are pure functions of eager upstream state and their own district's sub-stream, so they run in
  parallel without shared writes; by the laws the pool keeps CITY's p95 within 300 ms up to ≈ 5 200 buildings (≈ 17 700
  people), where a single worker holds it only up to ≈ 3 770, and moves the METROPOLIS one-second knee from ≈ 11 400 to
  ≈ 14 200 buildings (§12.5). M1 and M2b keep it primary only at the sizes where it measures faster than a single
  worker, with identical digests (§12.3; NR3-1).

## §13 Testing and verification

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r1); drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r1

*In plain words.* Five test benches run in continuous integration, in three tiers — a quick one on every change
(minutes), a full one every night (hours) and the largest runs at every milestone: random and deliberately awkward shapes
thrown at the geometry kernel (it must never crash or hang), a thousand towns per size and water setting (every rule
checked), up to a hundred thousand scripted edits (nothing lost, nothing overlapping, nothing outside the edit changed),
fixed "golden" seeds whose fingerprints must not change unless a release says why, and measurements of our towns against
numbers we measured from the references — read from one numbers-only file, never from the captures themselves. Every
acceptance number says what kind of evidence it is; the owner judges side-by-sides through a written, blind protocol;
every threshold has a number today and a stated way to confirm it.

### 13.1 Kernel property tests (fast-check; B-FUZZ) and the ladder coverage test

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3, fixall/draft-scope-r3

Every kernel primitive is fuzzed with two input families, held to one bar — **0 crashes, 0 hangs (hard timeout), 0
invalid outputs** — at the sizes of §13.8's tiers.

1. **Random inputs** (`fast-check`): concave, holed, thin, near-collinear, snapped, duplicated-vertex, ≥ 300-vertex and
   zero-area polygons and chains.
2. **Constructive degeneracies (GEO-12).** Random sampling almost never lands on an exact degeneracy — a line across a
   2²⁴ frame holds at most 2²⁴ of its 2⁴⁸ lattice points, so a random third point is collinear with probability
   ≤ 2⁻²⁴ — so every degenerate class is built on purpose from random parameters:
   * lattice points exactly on a segment, placed by gcd stepping (`p₀ + k · d / gcd(dx, dy)`);
   * collinear triples and collinear overlapping edges (shared runs from 1 cm to the whole edge, same and opposite
     direction);
   * cuts through a vertex and cuts grazing a reflex vertex (through it, and offset by 0 and ± 1 lattice unit);
   * antennae (chains dangling into a face) and chains touching a boundary at one point;
   * coincident typed chains — a wall on a bank, a quay on a shore, a street on a district boundary, a track on a field
     boundary;
   * rectangles, squares and regular n-gons (n = 3 … 12) rotated by random angles and snapped to the lattice;
   * holes touching the outer ring at a vertex and along an edge, and holes touching each other;
   * simultaneous skeleton events (regular polygons, equal-sided rectangles, symmetric notches);
   * values exactly on quantisation boundaries (half-centimetre ties before snapping; ± (2²³ − 1)) and values `snap`
     must refuse (± 2²³, NaN, ± ∞);
   * the attraction, move and kept-content cases (GEO-3, GEO-5, GEO-35, VK-1–VK-18): a vertex at (20, 20) against the
     edge (0, 0)–(1 000, 0) (it moves onto (0, 0); no sub-`minEdge` edge); a chain crossing an edge next to a vertex
     standing 25.0–25.7 cm from it; a stretch whose join point lies within `attractCm` of an edge endpoint; a `warp`
     with `fromLevel = 1` over a street ending on a shore (the junction slides along the shore and the step commits); a
     `pinch` that would shorten an edge below `minEdge` and a step that would put two vertices on one lattice point
     (both halve); a 20 × 10 m rectangle with a 3 × 2 m notch on a long side (skeleton path; no roof line outside); star
     rings of radius 2²³ − 2 (`area2` exact); an L1 lane into a face holding kept L3 content of an earlier stage
     (`E_KEPT`); a canal across a CITY district that cuts a lane whose remainder is pruned and re-routes a `primary` —
     every face outside its footprint (§4.11: the channel buffer ∪ every L1 cell its way rule touches) byte-identical
     except the seam exception at its boundary, and its L0 channel attracting onto exactly its prepared vertices (each
     promoted, no other finer vertex promoted, each deck carrying `deck` beside `way` in the form §2.2 rule 7 defines —
     the kept way's own L1 edge, no L0 edge across the channel, J-I12); a course-knot move and a river move across a
     street grid, with the same footprint and contact assertions (§7.3 (b)); a canal crossing a walled CITY's wall
     between two towers — no `E_KEPT` and no `E_LEVEL`, every face outside §4.11's footprint (the cells its buffer meets
     and its way rule touches, the old run's strip-line stretches and the new strips' ground included) byte-identical
     less the seam exception, every way the new strips meet cut at their boundary, the water gate's `Gate.banks` on its
     two `gate_end` vertices (NP3-2, pipeline round 4 X-S1); a carve chain that touches a finer edge away from its
     prepared vertices (`E_LEVEL` inside the clear region, `E_KEPT` outside; §3.3 clear regions); a lane removed from a
     spine it ended on (the spine's chain restored exactly, its own shape vertices untouched; the `split` flag, §2.2
     rule 3); II.1 (3)'s neighbour step beside finished plots — a plot-line end within `attractCm` of the foot
     (promoted; every plot ring unchanged), one farther (a kerb split; each ring equal to its prior ring with the vertex
     removed), and the street removed again (the kerb restored exactly), by an undo and by a reroll — at a promoted
     plot-line end and at a promoted footprint corner, the kerb's L2 route and digest, the block's and the plot's rings
     and the wing rings equal to those before the step (II.1 (3); NP3-5, pipeline round 4 X-S3); an S8 T-junction on a
     spine with a width profile (every sampled half-width unchanged); a pool overlay writing outside its district
     (`E_SCOPE`); a logged `moveVertex` replayed after an upgrade that puts an unrelated vertex 20 cm from its position
     (bound to the signature-matching vertex or orphaned, never to the unrelated one); a slot freed and reused inside a
     stage (the query returns the new item); a pooled district beside the settlement perimeter commits plot lines that
     end on the backland part's inner edge with 0 unresolved crossings at pool sizes 0 and 3, and every freeze finds
     every dynamic grid and tombstone set empty after its rebuild (§3.3 pool step 1); an L3 query in a block before and
     after S11 derives L4 there — two plots sharing their lowest-leftmost vertex with an L4 vertex on their shared edge
     — returns its results in the same order (`fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out` C); a `warp` over a spine carrying a
     same-level T-junction, then its lane removed (the junction stays as a shape vertex of the warped spine), and a
     `warp` that re-seats a Steiner vertex, then `clearFiner` (the vertex dissolves and the coarser edge is restored
     exactly); a warp moving a kerb beside a vertex 25.3 cm from it — the kerb (0, 0)–(1 000, 9) past (517, 30) —
     commits, its re-seated vertex placed by the placement rule (`fixall_kernel_r3_checks.out` A); a `warp` over a
     locked plot and over a pinned building (every corner held; a neighbour's footprint corner on the locked plot's line
     slides) and a `warp` with `fromLevel = 1` over finished fabric (0 `E_KEPT`); a way split between two width knots
     (every sampled half-width within 10⁻⁹ cm of its value before the split), then re-joined (the original profile bit
     for bit); the frozen copy sent to a pool worker holds typed arrays only — no `Map` or `Set` reachable from the
     message; and (kernel round 4, X-S1) a canal across an open enceinte's glacis line and a river moved through a
     walled town — every indexed role unique per ordinal (§3.10), the water gate's `Gate.banks` resolving to its two
     `gate_end` vertices, and no `anchor` contact name left after the edit; II.1 (3)'s neighbour step at a plot-line
     end, then the street removed by a reroll, not an undo — the kerb's L2 route, index and digest equal to those before
     the step; a river moved away from a quay-lined and a walled bank — the quay and wall edges back at L1, the L0 view
     land and water only, and a deck left over land at the way's level after F-REDERIVE (before it, at the level of its
     `deck_end` rows, with no L0 edge at it), its bank vertices unpinned; a warp that re-seats two Steiner vertices
     whose projections lie within `minEdge` + 1 cm of each other gives identical output after a slot renumbering (the
     two placement orders differ in 6.8 % of such pairs, `fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out` B); a stretch of a way removed
     between two junctions and a stretch of a ring removed between two anchors — the rest of each chain unchanged and
     every remaining profile sample within 10⁻⁹ cm of its value before (`fixall_kernel_r4_checks.out` C) — and a removal
     that leaves a way in two parts without a `rekey`, refused by role consistency; a promotion that leaves another
     finer vertex 1.2 cm from its new route edge commits with no `E_INVARIANT`, and every index query whose box meets
     that vertex returns it. And (kernel round 5): two neighbour steps on one kerb edge, the first street removed by a
     reroll — its plot-line end back at L3 and the kerb's L2 route equal to the route with only the second step
     (`fixall_kernel_r5_checks.out` A); a warp that moves a spine's vertices around an unmoved same-level T-junction,
     then its lane removed — the junction stays a shape vertex of the warped spine; a warp with `fromLevel = 1` over a
     generated and over an edited water gate — neither gate's bank vertices move; after a neighbour step and its removal
     by a reroll with no partition rebuilt in between, level-2 and level-3 queries over the kerb return exactly what
     they return after a rebuild, and a slot freed in one district and reused in another, the second district's
     partition rebuilt before the first's, is returned as its new item and never as its old one; a declared preparation
     batch placing two contact names on one entity, its ops permuted — identical ordinals; new water across a corner of
     the frame — the border's stretch between its two contact points, the corner included, unchanged and closed.

**Properties** (checked after every operation): output simple; nesting by index (every face inside its parent); no edge
shorter than `minEdge` from any writer, after every insertion and every warp step, and clearance ≥ `minEdge`; Euler
characteristic after every insertion; `remove(insert(x)) ≡ id` on the topology; **`splitFace` children tile the parent
exactly at the child level (integer `area2` equality)**; `mergeFaces ∘ splitFace` restores the ring and the id;
`corridorUnion` faces disjoint and covering; `offset(−d) ∘ offset(+d)` ⊆ original and `insetFace` empties monotonically;
**every straight-skeleton output passes the §3.8 validator — a connected graph inside the face whose number of
independent cycles equals the number of holes — or is a reported downgrade**; OBB contains the hull and collinear input
returns `E_DEGENERATE`; LIR inside the face; snap rounding idempotent and terminating within its bound; the `orient2d`
sign equal to a BigInt reference on adversarial triples; Poisson minimum distance ≥ r; differential agreement with the
CI oracles (Clipper2-WASM in Node, `polygon-clipping`) on booleans and buffers, split by attraction (§3.7): unattracted
cases with equal face counts and symmetric difference ≤ perimeter × 1 cm, attracted cases valid and within perimeter ×
√2 · `attractCm`, ≥ 10⁵ unattracted cases per operation; roles preserved on coincident chains (a sliver between a spine
and a shore keeps both); a declared batch's result identical under any permutation of its ops, and a callback-form
stage's identical across two runs, a slot renumbering and pool sizes 0–3 (§3.3); `clearFiner` after a refinement
restores the coarser level exactly; mandatory chains never rejected for precision; 0 stale references after every batch;
every index query's answer identical before and after a rebuild of the partitions it reads (§3.3; VK4-5); after every
removal each edge's level is the lowest among its rows and no vertex is coarser than every edge and role at it (§3.10's
level-consistency row); save → load → save byte-identical (§3.9); a 3 000 m relief fixture stores without a clamp and D8
is defined on 100 % of the hydrology grid's land cells over frame and margin (§2.3); every routine returns a typed
result on the pathological corpus.

**Ladder coverage (G-R9):** every rung of every ladder in §5.2 is reachable by a fixture, and each downgrade (medial
axis, the plain-roof downgrade, straight cut, substitution) is exercised; no roof line lies outside its footprint; a
skeleton failure is never a crash and never a visual surprise.

### 13.2 Per-stage invariants, statistics, cost-model tests, contract tests, B-EDIT

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3, fixall/draft-scope-r3

* **Invariants.** The §5.3 suite runs by scope — batch-local invariants per batch, stage-end invariants per stage,
  save / load invariants per document, CI-only invariants in the harness — on B-CITY (1 000 seeds × the 4
  `WaterSetting`s of §13.3 × 3 rungs in the nightly tier; 50 seeds per rung in the PR tier, §13.8; all three rungs from
  M1, because METROPOLIS generates from M1, §16). Each invariant has an id, a severity, a count in
  the report and a CI threshold: hard = 0 per 1 000 cities; soft within its band. The **digest-maintenance oracle**
  checks on every B-CITY-lite city that the Merkle digest maintained batch by batch equals a full recompute (§6.2).
* **The statistics record, split (SCL-21).** The **core record** is O(n) and is emitted by every generation within
  4 ms at CITY (§12.4): counts per entity kind and class; areas per class and band; fixed-bin histograms per district and
  band of plot area, frontage, depth, footprint area and storeys; way length per class; the junction-degree histogram;
  turning per 100 m on ways resampled at 10 m; the walled share and built extent; ladder uses per cause and rung; every
  requested feature's delivery tier (§5.1 principle 7); stage timings. The **bench metrics** — detour index over sampled
  destination pairs, Moran's I, KS distances, junction-to-junction runs, orientation coherence and wall alignment,
  figure-ground metrics on renders (§8.5), tree nearest-neighbour and pair-correlation statistics computed from §8.10's
  stamped scatter — run through `stats(doc, { level: 'bench' })` on demand or in the bench, never on the one-click path.
* **Cost-model tests (SCL-19; NF-S10).** Each stage is timed on **nine sizes — three per rung: the band's bottom, its
  target and its top** — 1 500, 5 000 and 9 900 (TOWN); 10 000, 20 000 and 29 900 (CITY); 30 000, 50 000 and 120 000
  (METROPOLIS) inhabitants, five seeds each (nightly; the METROPOLIS sizes are reported from M1 and gate from M2b, which
  measures and tunes METROPOLIS, §16; VS2-2).
  Its log-log slope of time against its declared work measure (the `Stage`'s work-limit laws, §5.1 (5), §14) must
  not exceed **1.15** for a stage declared linear and **1.25** for one declared n log n; §12.3's per-rung cost laws are
  fitted on the same runs. **Work limits follow population:** each run reports, per stage, the F-WORK hit rate (work
  cuts per 1 000 batches), and CI fails when the rate at the top of a band exceeds the rate at its bottom by more than
  1 per 1 000 — §5.1 (5)'s pre-decided coefficient fallback then applies and the sweep re-runs. **Per-edit cost against
  model size:** a fixed scope — one plot edit, one block reroll, one district regeneration — costs the same at TOWN, CITY
  and METROPOLIS within ± 20 % (§12.6), and so does per-edit validation (§5.3); both are measured TOWN → CITY from M2a
  and TOWN → METROPOLIS from M2b (§16). **Index work** is fitted against commits × level size (§3.3). A **memory test** per
  rung uses §12.8's definition — on generated towns from M1 (TOWN, CITY) and M2b (METROPOLIS), and from M2a on the
  reference 300-edit CITY document while it is load-verified with a district regeneration and a Re-derive from S3
  applied during it, at pool sizes 0 and 3 (§12.8, §16; VS3-1, VD3-5); a **document-size test** per rung holds ≤ 320 B per building at CITY (§2.9); the
  simulation module's occupancy (one hour for 50 000 people ≤ 50 ms in the worker, §10.3, §12.7) has its own cost-model
  test in the module's milestone (M4b). **First map by size (N-2):** B-CITY's browser runs time the first map at the
  same three sizes per rung — TOWN 1 500 / 5 000 / 9 900, CITY 10 000 / 20 000 / 29 900, METROPOLIS 30 000 / 50 000 /
  120 000 people — and fit §12.5's first-map laws (M1 for TOWN and CITY, M2b for METROPOLIS; nightly thereafter).
  The same runs pan and zoom during an A2 300-dpi export of a CITY: every settle within §12.5's bound, the export
  completed and byte-identical to the idle-view export and to one during which an edit is made (§8.9, §12.7; NR3-6).
  **The model max clause (NR-1, NR3-4):** every nightly B-CITY generation's model time ÷ its rung's law at its own
  building count is recorded as a screen; a generation above 1.25 is re-timed three times in §12.1's timing phase and
  fails the clause only when the median of its three ratios exceeds 1.25 (the 20 highest when more than 20 are flagged;
  §12.3), gating TOWN and CITY from M1 and METROPOLIS from M2b. Every gating timing — the sweeps, the first-map runs,
  §12.3's pool comparison and these re-timings — is taken in §12.1's timing phase and normalised by its calibration
  score (rendering round 4 S4).
* **Stage contract tests.** The same inputs and stream give the same digest on Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox and
  WebKit, with workers on and off and pool sizes 0–3 (G-P10); §6.5's determinism tests run beside them (time dilation ×
  10 and × 0.1, the derived-complete digest over three district orders — S12b and the hinterland unit included, replay =
  session, truncation identity, the host-provider double run, links and documents without their packs or host). S8's
  working block equals S9's committed block (Hausdorff 0; §3.7). The per-stop placement digests of §13.3 are the
  contract test of S13b; the stamp-tile asset's tiles hash to their stored values in the generation worker and the tile
  worker, and `plat/tools/stamptiles/` rebuilds the asset byte-identical on the five engines (§8.3; NR-6, NR3-7); a tile
  rastered whole and in 1-ms slices is pixel-identical (§8.3; NR3-2; rendering round 4 S5). A stop placed whole and
  placed one unit per step gives identical placement digests (§8.3, §9.2; NR4-2); the shipped stamp tiles pass the seam
  check — 0 point pairs closer than r₀ across cells in all 256 2 × 2 arrangements of each class's four tiles, for every
  band's rank subset (§8.3, §8.10; NR4-1). **View-data contracts:** every shipped style sheet loads at every band
  through §8.2's slot resolution with 0 unresolved and 0 ambiguous (semantic, pass) pairs (NR-3); entities with equal
  lineage in two seeds' towns get different render keys (§8.3; VD2-6), on two B-CITY-lite seeds per rung.
* **Stage property tests.** 10 000 coast / island / fjord / sky outlines per intent → 0 self-intersections and 0 untyped
  loops; 0 overlapping or self-intersecting plots on concave, notched and curved blocks before any fallback; attached
  and party-wall shares on curved-street blocks inside the dense band; roster `manifest(P₂) ⊇ manifest(P₁)` for P₂ > P₁
  on 1 000 seeds; the stage-3 contract (the union of composed wings equals the outline, §2.6); the `ringed` fixture (≥ 3
  closed rings, radius CV ≤ 10 %); a B-CITY sweep over `wealthLevel` ∈ {0, 0.5, 1} (population ± 5 %, walled share in
  band); the derived-complete digest identical across district orders; opening a person leaves the digest, the log and
  the undo stack unchanged; **0 `E_KEPT` on the one-click path** over B-CITY (a stage whose domain overlaps an earlier
  stage's kept content is a pipeline bug; VK-1); every gate and weld vertex on its trace, and stage 1's trace within 40

* **The faithfulness campaign (O9 c; §7.3 item 7 (iv); IMP-7, VS2-9).** New random is judged by a campaign, not per
  sequence. Each nightly run draws **n = 800 regenerated scopes** from its B-EDIT New-random events — 400 block scopes
  and 400 district scopes, by a seeded draw; a night whose B-EDIT run holds fewer than 400 New-random events of a kind
  adds New random on seeded scopes of that kind in its B-CITY-lite towns until it has 400 — and for each generates
  **K = 50 from-scratch references** of the same scope: the same upstream state and context, rerolls 32 768 + i for
  i = 0 … 49, a range no user reroll reaches, so no reference can coincide with the tested regeneration. For each of the
  four statistics (median plot area, median frontage width, density, attached share) the rank r of the regenerated value
  among the K references counts the references below it plus a uniform draw from 0 … t over the t references equal to
  it (the draw comes from the campaign's own stream), so r is exactly uniform on 0 … K for a perfect regenerator,
  whatever K and however discrete the statistic. The ranks are binned into 10 bins of ⌊r · 10 / (K + 1)⌋ with expected
  counts proportional to the number of rank values each bin holds; a χ² test per statistic gives four p-values, and the
  campaign **fails when Holm's procedure rejects at family-wise 0.01** (the smallest p-value below 0.0025). Cost
  ≈ 40 800 scope generations (800 × 51), ≈ 12.5 CPU-min at §12.6's block and district costs (20 400 × ≈ 6.6 ms +
  20 400 × ≤ 30 ms), inside the nightly tier's budget (§13.8).
  **Why 800 scopes (VS2-9).** A scope's four statistics move together — a denser block has smaller plots, narrower
  frontages and more attached houses — and correlated statistics add less evidence than independent ones: with them
  correlated at ρ = 0.8, a campaign of 400 scopes catches a +0.25 standard-deviation bias in only 92.2 % of nights and a
  regenerator 0.8 × too snug in 95.2 % (922 / 1 000 and 952 / 1 000; the round-2 verifier's independent re-implementation
  gave 92.0 % and 95.0 %), so with the re-run rule below a real fault would be declared on its first night only
  0.85–0.91 of the time. **Executed** at n = 800 (`docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r3_o9c_n800.py` → `.out`, own
  code, stdlib; each generation's four statistics share a scope component at ρ = 0, 0.8 and 1): a perfect regenerator
  fails 1.0 % of campaigns on continuous statistics (31 / 3 000 at ρ = 0.8, 15 / 1 500 at ρ = 0) and 1.4 % (14 / 1 000) on
  heavily tied, scope-varying discrete statistics; a +0.25 sd bias and a 0.8 × too-snug regenerator are caught in
  2 000 / 2 000 campaigns each at ρ = 0 and at ρ = 0.8 (95 % lower bound 99.8 %), a 0.6 × too-snug and a 1.5 × too-loose
  one in 500 / 500, and — at the degenerate ρ = 1, where the four statistics move as one — the bias in 99.3 % and the
  snugness in 99.7 %. Without the randomised tie-break a perfect regenerator fails every campaign on a tied statistic
  (`fixall_verify_scope_o9c_rank.out`). A failing statistic's histogram names the fault: a hump is too snug, a U too
  loose, a slope a bias. **A failed campaign is re-run once with the next campaign seed**: a perfect regenerator fails
  two in a row with probability ≈ 1–2 × 10⁻⁴, and a fault of the sizes above is declared on the night it first runs with
  probability ≥ 0.996 at ρ ≤ 0.8 (≥ 0.985 at ρ = 1). A second failure is a regeneration defect — entered in
  `known-defects.json`, and M3a does not exit until it is fixed (§16), because no threshold can be relaxed without
  passing a wrong regenerator.
* **Control sweeps.** §7.8's statistical monotonicity and continuity: 21 steps × 50 seeds at TOWN and CITY (nightly);
  METROPOLIS in the milestone tier. The population control's sweep also reports the F-WORK hit rate per stage, which
  must stay flat across each band as above.
* **Option-interaction matrix.** Every pair of toggles rendered and diffed; no option silently disables another (O12 c).
* **Documentation coverage (COV-FTG-A25).** 100 % of controls and entity kinds have a guide anchor (§14 `@plat/docs`);
  every in-app help link resolves (CI link check); the release notes list every open entry of `known-defects.json`.

### 13.3 Seed goldens with the declared-shift protocol (G-P11, G-R9), from M1

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3; drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r3

A golden suite of 12 seeds × {TOWN, CITY, METROPOLIS} × the four `WaterSetting`s {`none`, `coast`, `river`,
`coast+river`} stores, per stage, its
**stage-isolated digest** (the stage's new code run on the previous output version's frozen upstream outputs, §6.4), its
entity counts, the core statistics record and one PNG per LOD and preset; and, per shipped preset's label style, a
**per-stop placement digest** (below). A release either matches or declares:

* a **shift record** for every stage whose isolated digest moved — the stage, the cause (a rule-table change, a fix, a
  new concern), the seeds and statistics that moved, the expected direction, and the output version the release creates;
* a **cascade record** for every end-to-end golden it re-signs, listing each downstream stage that moved and showing,
  from the isolated goldens, that each moved only through its inputs; a downstream stage whose isolated digest also
  moved needs its own shift record, so an unrelated regression cannot ride on an upstream shift.

An undeclared move fails CI; a declared statistic that moves against its declared direction fails CI until the record
states why; only declared stages are re-signed; stages untouched by a release stay byte-identical (O2 e). A same-seed
output change is never let ride silently (owner non-negotiable 10).

**The records are product files (NF-S1).** Everything the golden gate and the release-notes generator read lives inside
`plat/`, so §17.1 (3)'s path rule and the gate never collide:

```ts
// @plat/testkit — the golden store and its records; JSON with a schema, committed in plat/goldens/
type WaterSetting = 'none'|'coast'|'river'|'coast+river';   // the one spelling of a water setting: B-CITY, the golden store, every record (VS2-5)
// a seed in a record is a Seed (u32, §2.9) written as its decimal string, e.g. "1221236157"; permalinks write it in base 36 (§6.4)
interface ShiftRecord {
  id: string; release: string /* generator version */; outputVersion: string | null /* the o<k> it creates; null for a view shift (S13b, render.stampTiles) */;
  stage: StageId | 'S13b' | 'render.stampTiles' /* view shifts: placement digests (S13b) and stamp-tile hashes (§8.10) */;
  cause: { kind: 'table'|'fix'|'concern'|'engine'|'feature'|'calibration'|'baselineShift'; ref: string /* table id@version, issue, concern id, CalibrationRun id, baseline id */; note: string };
  seeds: { seed: string; rung: Rung; water: WaterSetting; before: Hash128; after: Hash128 /* isolated stage digest, or the placement digest for S13b */ }[];
  statistics: { metric: string /* core-record field or §13.5 metric id */; rung: Rung; before: number; after: number; expected: 'up'|'down'|'none'|'any' }[];
  tiles?: { tile: string /* class, tile index (§8.10) */; before: Hash128; after: Hash128 }[] /* render.stampTiles shifts only; their seeds list is empty, the library being seed-independent */;
  d5SeedsChanged: string[] /* seeds of any D-5 panel (§13.6) whose render moved */; milestone: string; date: string; author: string }
interface CascadeRecord {
  id: string; outputVersion: string; upstream: string[] /* ShiftRecord ids that explain it */;
  downstream: { stage: StageId; before: Hash128; after: Hash128 /* end-to-end digests */; isolatedUnchanged: true /* otherwise the stage needs its own ShiftRecord */ }[];
  seeds: string[]; date: string }
interface MilestoneRecord {
  milestone: string; date: string; outputVersions: string[] /* created during the milestone */; shifts: string[]; cascades: string[];
  parity: string /* plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json — the ParityReport the exit is judged on, §13.5 (VS2-5) */;
  d5: { status: D5Status; record: string /* plat/goldens/d5/<milestone>/record.json, §13.6 */ } | null;
  knownDefects: { opened: string[]; closed: string[] }; exitCriteria: { id: string; result: 'pass'|'fail'|'fallback-applied'; evidence: string }[] }
```

* `plat/goldens/store/o<k>/` holds, per seed and stage, the frozen upstream outputs and the digests, counts, statistics
  and placement digests; PNGs are stored content-addressed in `plat/goldens/png/` (large-file storage) and referenced by
  hash.
* `plat/goldens/shifts/o<k>.json` holds the shift and cascade records that created output version o<k>;
  `plat/goldens/shifts/view/<release>.json` holds a release's view shifts (S13b and `render.stampTiles`).
* `plat/goldens/milestones/<milestone>.json` is each milestone's exit record.
* The golden CLI refuses a record with a missing field; the release-notes generator of `@plat/docs` reads only these
  files and `plat/docs/known-defects.json`.
* `docs/validation/shifts/<milestone>.md` and `docs/validation/d5/<milestone>.md` are **research-side copies** generated
  from these files by `research/baselines/mirror_records.py` (research may read the product; the product never reads
  research); no CI job reads them, and a hand edit there changes nothing.

**Placement digests (N-24; §9.1's cross-engine promise).** For every golden town, every shipped preset's label style and
each of B-ZOOM's 27 zoom stops, S13b places the band's area and way labels for all candidates and the addresses and
repeated street names of the default view's visible tiles (§9.2's scope); the placement digest hashes, per candidate in
id order, the label id, the chosen alternate (or *yielded*), the ladder rung, the size and every glyph's position and
angle as exact IEEE doubles — placement uses only + − × ÷, `Math.sqrt` and `dmath` on the fonts' integer metrics and the
stop's scale, and `@plat/labels` is held to §6.5's allowlist lint like a model package. So are the inputs S13b reads
from the renderer (VS2-4): every implementation of `ObstacleSource` and `RoleIndex`, every function they call and the
S14 code that writes the display-list columns they read — `bbox`, the geometry ranges and `GeomTable`, `layer` and `z`,
and the symbol extents computed from the style sheet's sizes (§6.5 (3), §14). Equal code on equal inputs then gives
equal bits on every engine; the rest of `@plat/render` (paint programs, backends, compositing) stays outside the lint,
because its output is pixels, compared by visual regression (§13.4), not by bit identity. The PR tier compares the
digests on Node x86 against the store; the nightly tier compares them on all five engines with workers on and off. A
digest that moves while every model digest holds is a **view shift**: it needs a `ShiftRecord` with stage `S13b` and
`outputVersion: null`, bumps no output version (placement is view data, §9.1) and bumps the style version of every
shipped sheet whose placements moved, because the style version is the axis that carries pixel identity (§6.4). A digest
that differs between engines is a determinism defect and fails the nightly run. The stamp-tile asset's stored hashes
(§8.10) are kept with the placement digests; a release whose asset moves a stored hash while every model digest holds is
a view shift of the same kind — a `ShiftRecord` with stage `render.stampTiles` and `outputVersion: null`, bumping the
style version of every shipped sheet that draws stamped classes (NR-6, NR3-7); an asset that only adds a new class's
tiles moves no stored hash and needs no record.

**From M1 (LC-19).** The output-version stamp, the shift, cascade and milestone records and the stage-isolated golden
tooling are built at M1, not at hardening (§16). Every milestone from M1 on writes its `MilestoneRecord` — each output
version created, its shift records, the D-5 panel seeds that changed — and a milestone cannot exit with an undeclared
shift. **Preview links:** until M4's exit fixes output version 1, every permalink and document made by the app is marked
*preview* — the app shows "preview: made with output version oN; a later release may draw this seed differently and
will say so" — and the link carries its `o=` (§6.4). Retention of output versions N−1 and N−2 (§6.4) is built and its
replay test passes at M3a; from then on a link inside the window replays exactly and one outside it opens with §6.4's
notice.

A nightly cross-platform golden run (Node x86 / arm64, Chromium, Firefox, WebKit; workers on and off; pool sizes 0 and
3) is the reproducibility proof: identical model digests per stage, identical derived-complete digests and identical
placement digests on every engine; and, from M3a (the GeoJSON exporter's milestone), the strict GeoJSON of one golden
CITY seed (`coast+river`) with its trees — §8.10's integer-centimetre instance positions with their species, crown
diameters and leaf types — byte-identical on every engine, workers on and off (§11.1; NR4-3).

### 13.4 Visual regression, B-ZOOM and the app harness

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r4); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r2; drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r2

* **Visual regression.** Playwright renders the golden suite per preset, LOD and backend; SSIM / `pixelmatch` against
  the stored PNG with a per-preset threshold; the draw-style census of §8.3 per preset; a "no fills" and a "no outlines"
  render must remain legible (R13).
* **B-ZOOM** (1:50 000 → 1:500, the default view of every rung): legibility floors and no feature popping more than once
  (footprint hash identical across bands); §8.3's checks — hairline fidelity, decoration stability, role continuity
  across band switches, no tree mark over a tier-1/2 casing, no casing pixels in junction mouths, the contrast matrix on
  the rendered city band; §9.4's label checks — floors, every node of the city cut (min(N_q, number of districts), §4.5)
  labelled at or above the floor and within ± 1 of MFCG's 9 / 12 / 18 at the matched sizes (NF-P9), 0 collisions at
  settled views and through a scripted zoom sweep, the pin pass's fixture — two pins brought together by a warp and two
  by a rename that lengthens the earlier pin's text: 0 collisions at every stop, the later pin reported hidden where the
  boxes meet, and the placement digests identical after a replay (§9.2; NR3-3) — and every placed glyph's text / halo
  pair at the label floor (§9.4); the draw-order census (the logged (slot, pass) sequence non-decreasing, §8.3);
  decoration stability for stamped, `grid` and `line` classes; the reload and two-derivation-order pixel identity of
  render-time keys (§8.3); §8.5's figure-ground metrics — street-edge recoverability against MFCG's value on its matched
  plain sweep renders (measured at M-1, §13.5), access-critical ways drawn ≥ 95 %.
* **Role continuity by family and milestone (VIS-9; N-23).** §8.2's rule — every shipped family defines all four bands
  and the mean roof and mean ground colours move by ΔE2000 < 2 across every band switch — is checked for a family from
  the milestone that ships its four bands: `ink` and `lit` from M2b (M1 ships `ink`'s city and district bands only, and
  B-ZOOM checks that one switch from M1), `hatched` from M5, the ink-family variants from M3b (§16).
* **The app harness** (Playwright, the reference machine of §12.1):
  * **Scripted tasks (O16 c; IMP-11)** — share a view link, export a layered SVG, change the coast side, see five
    variants of one kind, recover from a mistaken regenerate, measure a street with the ruler, find a named building
    through the gazetteer: each passes when it completes in the stated number of UI actions (one action where a
    reference needs a detour; recovery = one undo) with every app response ≤ 1 s, run on every PR.
  * **Accessibility (COV-FTG-A24)** — axe-core on every screen and panel of `@plat/app` reports 0 serious or critical
    violations; every control is reachable and operable by keyboard alone in a scripted run with visible focus; every
    scripted task above also passes keyboard-only; the gazetteer list and search and the "features in view" list reach
    every building, plot, district and pinned person without the canvas.
  * **Input scheme** — every binding of the default `keymap.json` (§14) fires its action while the map has focus and
    none fires while a text field has focus; a user-edited keymap round-trips through save and load.

### 13.5 Reference-parity metrics (B-REF), read from one numbers-only baseline file

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r2; drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r2

The `parity` CLI in `@plat/testkit` reads **only** `baselines.json` — our own measurements of the references, numbers
only, generated research-side by scripts under `research/baselines/` from the captures and committed into
`plat/packages/testkit/baselines/` (§17, D-29) — and our B-CITY outputs, and reports every metric against its band. It
never opens `captures/`, `research/` or `reference/`.

```ts
interface Baseline {
  id: string; metric: string; unit: string;
  reference: 'MFCG' | 'FTG' | 'NG' | 'VG' | `corpus:${string}`;       // corpus rows arrive through §13.9
  referenceBuild: string;            // itch build, FTG server date + create-request hash, NG / VG build — required (COV-VG-VN-010)
  capture: string; script: string; date: string;                       // provenance: capture folder, research-side script, run date
  matched?: { rung: Rung; mfcgSize?: number; ftgSize?: 'BIG_TOWN' | 'BIG_CITY' | 'CITY' | 'METROPOLIS'; population?: number };
  role: 'target' | 'weakness' | 'descriptive';                        // what the reference number means for us (FTG-15)
  values: { p10?: number; p50?: number; p90?: number; n: number; seeds: number } | { bins: number[]; histogram: number[]; n: number; seeds: number };
}
interface ParityReport {                 // written by the parity CLI per run (NF-S1); read by milestone exits, §13.9's CalibrationRun and the release notes
  runId: string; date: string; outputVersion: string; generatorVersion: string; baselines: Hash128 /* hash of the baselines.json it read */;
  rows: { metric: string; baselineIds: string[]; role: Baseline['role']; rung: Rung; preset?: string;
    band: { lo?: number; hi?: number; ksMax?: number; direction?: 'above'|'below'; margin?: number };
    ours: { p10?: number; p50?: number; p90?: number; ks?: number; n: number; seeds: number };
    verdict: 'pass'|'fail'|'reported' /* descriptive rows are always 'reported' */; note?: string }[];
  summary: { pass: number; fail: number; reported: number } }
```

Each milestone's parity report is stored as `plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json` and named in its `MilestoneRecord`
(§13.3).

The CLI refuses a row without `referenceBuild`, `capture`, `script` or `date`. A new reference build never overwrites a
row: it adds a row (the id gains the build) and is a **declared baseline shift** in the milestone's shift record, so a
silently drifting reference build (VG changed geometry for the same seed between builds 19251041 and 19365073) can
never move a gate unnoticed. Rows hold numbers, units and provenance only — no names, colours, grammars or code.

**The band rule (DEF-1; IMP-6).** Every row below has its band rule and its provenance now; a reference number marked
**⟨M-1⟩** is measured by M-1 (§16), which lists every such measurement. **The ⟨M-1⟩ rule (NF-S5):** if M-1 cannot
measure an ⟨M-1⟩ number — the capture lacks the feature, or the measurement is not reproducible across seeds — that
reference cell becomes *descriptive*, gates nothing, and enters `known-defects.json` with the reason; the parity CLI
reports an ⟨M-1⟩ cell without its baseline row as *fail*, never as *pass*. *Target* rows pass when ours lies
in [p10 × 0.9, p90 × 1.1] of the reference's seed spread (a single-value baseline: ± 15 %), and distributions when our
KS distance to the reference is ≤ 1.25 × the reference's own seed-to-seed KS distance at p90. *Weakness* rows are
one-sided: ours must beat the reference in the declared direction by the stated margin. *Descriptive* rows are reported
beside ours and gate nothing. The bands below are this rule applied to today's baselines; when M-1 re-measures a
baseline (five seeds per matched MFCG size, FTG's new captures), the band is recomputed by the same rule with provenance
"M-1 ⟨date⟩", and a recomputation that turns a passing gate into a failing one is declared in the shift record.
Thresholds no reference can set are §13.7's.

**Matched sizes (MN-2; §12.2, §13.6).** TOWN ↔ MFCG size 40 and FTG BIG_TOWN; CITY ↔ MFCG size 80 and FTG BIG_CITY;
METROPOLIS ↔ MFCG size 130 (FTG per D-31). MFCG numbers come from its plain-option size sweep (walls, citadel, plaza and
temple on; shanty town, parks, river and coast off; its JSON export is in metres, the internal unit 4.00 m). **Curves
(FTG-15)** are measured after both sides are resampled at a 10 m arc-length step, so neither FTG's 25–40 m placement
steps nor PLAT's smoothed vertex spacing enters a number.
