the widening where the components are built — M1 + 2 / + 3 (with the generated-town format moved in from M2a), M3a + 1 /
+ 1, M2a unchanged (the format out, the records digest in) — so they still sum to the total. **A later pass that adds
build work prices it here:** its scope seat names each new mechanism with the line that absorbs it, or widens a line by
an itemised amount and keeps the milestone rows equal to the total.

*Chose* to state the larger, honest total *over* keeping 100–130 by cutting scope *because* the owner asked that nothing
be deferred and that everything be fixed as soon as possible, and the earlier figure left out the content, the app and
the rig that the base contains. The cuts that would shrink it are recorded for the owner's veto, not applied: the
module M4b (8–14 pw); VTT, glTF / OBJ, CityJSON and the CBOR twin (≈ 3–5 pw); all but three forms (≈ 2–3 pw); the
should-have "full" tiers (4–6 pw) — together a base of ≈ 122–158 pw and a total of ≈ 136–176 pw.

The riskiest items, in order: the fusion timing and statistics on real terrain (M0 c, M1); the bent-cut engine on
concave and holed faces (M0 b); the kernel's own booleans and bands (M0 a, with Clipper2-WASM as the pre-decided single
engine, §3.7); the straight skeleton's robustness (M0 a); the content authoring cost (M1, M2b, M4b — CONFIDENCE §3.4's
re-pricing is the warning); the thin CITY budget headroom (§12); the D-5 protocol's dependence on the owner's time
(§13.6's rater rule answers it: an unrated panel never stops the build and never lets a gate be claimed).

**Staged by the owner (hooks concrete; documented, not bugs to re-find):** stage-3 building compositions (§2.6's
`outline` / `compose` split, cost contract and intake measurement); the village product THORP → HAMLET → VILLAGE (PART
III); sewers and floating islands (II.6); the evolution engine beyond the one built growth path (§4.11); calibration
against the historical corpus (§13.9); SettlementForge inputs (§11.4's host-input contract). Nothing else is out of
scope: CityJSON is built (§11.1), the host-input contract is decided (§11.4), sharing needs no hosted service (§11.5),
setting packs have their format (§10.4), there is no WASM kernel (§3.7), and the relief tier is a base program (§8.2).

## §17 Clean-room and legal posture; third-party licences

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r1); drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r1

*In plain words.* We never copy or port the references' code (the 2017 open-source ancestor is GPL and the live builds
are proprietary); we re-implement published ideas and the behaviour we measured. Their name lists, palettes, building
tables and textures are their creative content and are never reused; ours are written fresh. The people who write the
product read only this document and a cleaned digest of the research, never the research itself; the product lives in
its own folder that cannot reach the research folders; reference numbers reach the tests through one numbers-only file;
and a scanner stops the build if a reference word list, palette or table turns up. Every library has a permissive
licence, is pinned and is credited in a generated notices file, so the owner can choose any licence for our own code.

### 17.1 The clean-room chain (IMP-1; D-29)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r5; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4, drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r4; earlier revision fixall/integrate-r3, fixall/draft-scope-r3

1. **Who reads what.** *Research seats* (readers, measurers, the digest writer) may read the findings, `captures/`,
   `research/` and — under the standing ruling — `reference/`. *Implementer seats* (anyone writing code, tables, style
   sheets, content, assets or tests in `plat/`) read only `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, the implementer digest in
   `plat/docs/digest/`, the `plat/` repository, published algorithm papers and the public documentation of adopted
   libraries; they never open `research/`, `captures/`, `reference/`, the findings, the critics, `docs/confidence/`,
   `docs/improvements/`, `docs/CONFIDENCE.md`, `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` or the red-team files. The citations in this
   document are for traceability; an implementer follows them only into the digest. No code from TownGeneratorOS
   (GPL-3), the FTG Foundry module or any captured bundle is read for implementation, ported or paraphrased.
2. **The implementer digest.** A digest seat writes `plat/docs/digest/` from the research: behaviours, measured numbers
   (each with its `baselines.json` id or finding reference) and the creators' stated ideas — no code excerpts, no
   reference word lists, grammars, palettes, tables or identifiers. A separate checker seat, which reads only the digest,
   runs the content scan below on it and files a report with it; every change to the digest repeats the check. This
   document is held to the same rule (FTG-22). The hashed scan of (5) needs the deny-list that M-1 builds, so until then
   **every seat that writes this document — a fix-all integration seat, an amendment pass's apply and repair lanes, any
   finishing or repair seat — runs, before its change lands,** the scripted document checks of
   `docs/validation/bench/doc_checks.py` (VS2-8, VS2-1), from the project root:
   `python3 docs/validation/bench/doc_checks.py --sections "⟨every section heading key the change touched⟩"` — the
   content checks (iii) and (vi) over the sections the change touched, the others over the whole document:
   (i) *identifiers* — a whole-word, case-sensitive search for the backticked identifiers of
   `research/findings/ftg-payload-visual.md` §7.2 and the one further time-setting message name the round-2 scan
   added — 36 names, which the script reads from the finding or holds research-side, so none is copied into this
   document;
   (ii) *colours* — every six-digit colour value of the document (`#rrggbb` or `0xrrggbb`) looked up, case-insensitive
   and hex-delimited, in `research/` (its text files, JSON included), `captures/**/README*.md`, `captures/**/*.json`
   (VS3-4), `docs/confidence/`, `docs/improvements/`, `docs/CONFIDENCE.md` and `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`;
   (iii) *token 3-grams* — the lower-cased word tokens of the changed sections against every 3-gram of
   `research/findings/*.md` and (VS3-4) of the string keys and values of every JSON file under `research/` and
   `captures/` — FTG's content database and every capture body included — taken in document order with purely numeric
   tokens dropped; a hit is a run of three or more consecutive shared 3-grams (five or more tokens in a row that also
   stand together in a finding or a capture) — the size at which a copied list, table row, grammar line or palette
   shows, while a single shared 3-gram ("per 100 m") is ordinary phrasing;
   (iv) *tables* — outside fenced code (a fence may be indented, as inside a list item) every line that starts with `|`
   ends with `|`, no other line sits between two table lines (VS2-1: a table row split over several lines renders as
   broken rows), and every row has its header's number of cells, counting only unescaped pipes (VS4-1: GitHub-flavoured
   Markdown splits a cell at every unescaped `|`, inside a code span too, and drops the cells beyond the header's count,
   so a bare pipe in code silently cuts the row short — inside a table write it `\|`, which the renderer shows as `|`);
   (v) *pointers* — every `§n` and `§n.m` pointer resolves to a heading of this document;
   (vi) *lists, in any order* (VS3-4) — a 3-gram needs the list's order, so a list pasted alphabetised shares none with
   its source: every JSON file under `research/` and `captures/` except the profiler's recordings (call censuses,
   coverage, idle, trace, draw and path records, run reports, metadata, session and index files — code identifiers and
   events, which (i) and (iii) cover) is read for its lists — a dict's keys, an array of strings, one field's string
   values across three or more records — and a hit is a line of the changed sections holding five or more distinct
   whole words of four or more letters that are members of one such list, reported as those words, sorted.
   Each hit is corrected before the change lands or reviewed: a reviewed hit is entered in
   `docs/validation/doc-checks-allow.tsv` with its check, its exact text and a written reason (a capture-citation file
   name, a measured number, a creator's sentence under 15 words quoted for traceability, ordinary phrasing, generic
   vocabulary in our own selection and order, a pointer into another document). The script exits non-zero while any hit
   is unreviewed, the change does not land until it exits zero, and the seat records its counts in its output file (a
   fix-all pass in its integration log, an amendment pass in `docs/validation/amendments-applied.md` and
   `amendments-repair.md`). From M-1 the hashed scan of (5) — whose list sets do (vi)'s work on salted digests — also runs
   over this document and replaces (i)–(iii) and (vi); (iv) and (v) stay. *Calibration (executed).* On §13–§17 as they
   stood after round 2 (lines 6657–7826 of the pre-round-3 text, md5 `ca2e2066…`, committed as
   `docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r4_calib_pre_r3_s13_s17.txt`), 1 196 of 26 236 token 3-grams are shared with the
   findings and they form **47 runs of five or more tokens (45 distinct; §13 24, §14 4, §15 11, §16 6, §17 2)** —
   measured numbers, ordinary phrases and one quoted creator sentence — a hand review of minutes; no run threshold from
   1 to 7 gives the 27 an earlier draft stated (VS3-5; `docs/validation/bench/fixall_verify_scope_r3_cleanroom_checks.out`
   part C, `fixall_scope_r4_cleanroom.out` part A). On the round-3 text the same rule gives 53 runs over §13–§17. (ii)
   finds none of the document's 36 colour values in its sources, the capture JSON included; (iv) found exactly the one
   broken row VS2-1 names, and its cell-count clause, run over the round-4 text, exactly one more — J-I15, whose bare
   pipe inside code hid its reasoning (VS4-1; `fixall_verify_scope_r4_checks.out` part C, `fixall_scope_r5_checks.out`). The round-4 extension, run over the whole round-3 text (2 052 JSON files, ≈ 30–45 s): the JSON
   corpus adds 50 distinct run texts to (iii) — ordinary phrasing the creators' posts and comments also hold, six of them
   lengthened forms of runs reviewed before — and (vi) flags 8 lines of generic vocabulary; each was reviewed into the
   allow file's round-4 block, so the extension adds no unreviewed hit to unchanged text. Of 429 lists in FTG's content
   database written as one line of five or ten names, (vi) catches all 429 in either order, while (iii) catches none of
   the alphabetised five-name lines and 210 of those in the database's order (`fixall_scope_r4_cleanroom.out` parts B–D).
   *Chose* scripted proxies with a reviewed allow file *over* a hand-run grep *because* round 2's hand-run proxy checked
   identifiers only and so passed any pasted palette or table while the rule read as satisfied (VS2-8); *chose* to bind
   every seat that writes this document *over* the integration seat alone *because* an amendment pass's lanes write it
   directly (VS2-8; J-S32); *chose* the list check (vi) beside the extended 3-gram check *because* a reordered list
   shares no 3-gram with its source (J-S35).
3. **The repository boundary.** The product is its own repository, `plat/`, at the root of this folder, outside
   `research/`, `captures/` and `reference/`. A PR-tier CI rule fails any import specifier, fixture path, script path or
   build input that resolves outside `plat/` (symbolic links resolved). The product's CI never reads the research trees.
4. **Reference numbers only through committed numbers-only files.** Research-side scripts (`research/baselines/`)
   measure the captures and write numbers with provenance (§13.5's `Baseline` rows); the file, `baselines.json`, is
   committed into `plat/packages/testkit/baselines/`, and the parity CLI reads only it. The D-5 panel is assembled
   research-side from the product's PNG exports and the capture images (§13.6); its only inputs to the product are two
   numbers-only files committed the same way into `plat/goldens/d5/⟨milestone⟩/` — `ftg-captures.json` (capture ids,
   rungs, water settings, resident counts) and `ng-counts.json` (NG hoods' building counts) — and `plat d5 seeds` reads
   only them (§13.6 (2); VS4-4).
5. **The content scan.** Research-side, `research/baselines/make_denylist.py` builds the deny-list from the creative
   data the findings and captures record — the references' naming-grammar rule names and terminal words, Markov and
   corpus sample words, palette colour values, FTG's building-type, profession, item and service identifiers and names,
   FTG's Foundry-module message and field names (FTG-22), and texture and image file hashes. The list holds only salted
   SHA-256 digests: of single normalised tokens (lower-cased, diacritics stripped) that are not in the spell-check word list §9.6 already needs,
   of token 3-grams in list order (so a copied table is caught even when every word in it is ordinary), of exact six-digit
   colour values, of file bytes, and — for every list the findings and captures record (a dict's keys, an array of
   strings, one field's values across records) — the set of salted digests of its members' words of four or more
   letters (S4-1), so a list copied in another order is still found. `@plat/testkit`'s clean-room scanner digests the
   same way every token of `@plat/tables`, assets, source string literals and comments and the digest, in the PR tier,
   and flags as a list hit any line, or any column of a table, that holds five or more distinct words of one list's
   set; a hit fails the build unless an allow entry with a written reason is reviewed and added — an authored roster
   that shares ordinary building or trade names with a reference list is such an entry, and the review decides whether
   the selection was copied. At every milestone the checker seat also runs a
   research-side palette audit: a shipped palette with three or more colours within ΔE2000 2 of one reference palette
   fails and is redesigned. Every file in `plat/assets` names the script that generated it or its third-party licence
   (fonts); a file with neither fails the build.
6. **Honest provenance.** Every table cell's provenance names where its number came from: `own`, `ref:⟨reference⟩
   ⟨behaviour⟩` (a measured or stated behaviour of a reference, admissible as a calibration anchor — for example the
   castle's 0.75 compactness gate (MFCG), 40 m bridge spacing and 39 m tower spacing (FTG), NG's lane-width law, Poisson
   k = 50), `owner`, `owner-eye ⟨milestone⟩`, `architecture ⟨date⟩`, `corpus` or `host`. A number that describes a
   behaviour is a fact; a list, grammar, palette or table is creative content and is never reused.
7. **The record.** `plat/docs/CLEAN-ROOM.md` holds the rule, the seat ledger (which seat read which research file, from
   the lane logs), the digest checker's reports and the deny-list's generation record (date, sources, counts — never the
   tokens).
8. **Sources of algorithms.** Published: Shewchuk predicates; snap rounding (Hobby; Guibas–Marimont; Hershberger);
   arrangement booleans by winding number; Bridson Poisson-disc; Felkel–Obdržálek and Aichholzer straight skeletons;
   Chaikin; Visvalingam–Whyatt; Parish–Müller growth; Lloyd relaxation; marching squares; priority-flood;
   Garbrecht–Martz flat resolution; fBm, with ridged multifractal noise and domain warping (Musgrave, in Ebert et al.,
   *Texturing and Modeling*, 3rd ed. 2003; §3.1). With the round-2 and round-3 text (NR-10): the xoshiro128\*\* generator
   (Blackman–Vigna, public domain; §6.1) with Irwin–Hall sums for its normal draws; MurmurHash3's x86 128-bit hash and
   its 32-bit finaliser (Appleby, public domain; H128 in §6.2, `RH32` in §8.1, `H32` in §13.6), checked against the
   SMHasher verification values; Krüger's transverse Mercator series in Karney's formulation, to fourth order in the
   third flattening (Krüger 1912; Karney 2011; §11.1); the van der Corput radical inverse and Morton (Z-order) bit
   interleaving for §8.10's progressive grid ranks; Ulichney's void-and-cluster ranking (1993; §8.10); the monotone-chain
   hull (Andrew) and rotating calipers (Toussaint) for the OBB (§3.1); centripetal Catmull–Rom splines and pinned-vertex
   Laplacian smoothing (§3.1, §4.2, §9.3); Dijkstra's and A\* shortest paths (§3.1, §4.2, §4.3); Brandes' betweenness
   (§4.3); Kruskal's spanning tree (§9.3); Lambert shading (§8.2's hillshade); CIELAB and the CIEDE2000 colour
   difference (Sharma–Wu–Dalal; §8.2). With the round-4 text (VS3-3): D8 steepest-descent flow directions and flow
   accumulation (O'Callaghan and Mark 1984; §2.3, §4.2 S1); the exact Euclidean distance transform in linear time
   (Felzenszwalb and Huttenlocher 2012; §4.5, §12.4); the three-pass box-filter approximation of a Gaussian (Wells
   1986; §4.5, §12.4); the Merkle hash tree (Merkle 1987; §6.2, D-28); context-free grammar expansion in the style of
   Tracery (Compton, Kybartas and Mateas 2015) and character n-gram Markov chains (Shannon 1948) for §10.4's naming
   engine — ideas only, with our own grammar and corpora; power diagrams (Aurenhammer 1987) with area targets
   (Aurenhammer, Hoffmann and Aronov 1998) for the hinterland lots of §4.9; Kahn's topological sort (1962) with the stage
   id as tie-break for the stage order (§4.1, §4.12); SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) for (5)'s salted digests. For the tests:
   Pearson's χ² test with Holm's step-down procedure (§13.2), Spearman's rank correlation, Moran's I,
   Kolmogorov–Smirnov distances and SSIM (Wang et al.; §13.4, §13.5); the pair-correlation function of a point pattern
   (Stoyan and Stoyan 1994; §4.9, §13.2, §13.5); Shannon's entropy (1948) for the heading and use-mix entropies (§13.5,
   §13.7); the Jaccard index (intersection over union; §6.3, §7.5); and the Hausdorff distance (§3.7, §13.2, II.5). The
   round-4 list was checked against the text by a scripted scan of 119 method names
   (`docs/validation/bench/fixall_scope_r4_methods.out`). An implementer reads each in its published form; the seat ledger of (7)
   records which. The creators' *stated* ideas: twisted bisection, the casing idiom, skeleton labels, the proposal queue,
   dependency ratios, lazy people, integer centimetres — with constants calibrated on our own measurements.
9. **Protocol names (FTG-22).** The host bridge's vocabulary is our own (§11.3): the concurrency token is `logHead`
   (§2.9), carried as `baseLogHead` and `currentLogHead`; time is the view key `time`, set by `view.set`, and the
   simulation module advances it with its own command `sim.advance { hours }` (§10.3, §11.3). Schema-level ideas — an
   event / command split, an optimistic-concurrency token — are admissible as ideas; the FTG module's message, command and
   field names are not reused, are in the deny-list, and occur nowhere in this document (check (i) of (2)).

### 17.2 Fonts (IMP-15)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r2); drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r2

Fonts are third-party assets under the SIL Open Font License and sit outside the clean-room rule: they are neither the
references' code nor their creative data. *Chose* IM FELL Great Primer (OFL) as the default label face *over* a
different serif chosen "for clean-room distance" *because* it is the face of MFCG's labels and part of the ink look the
owner adopted (D-1), and clean-room distance applies to the references' code and content, not to a public OFL font;
EB Garamond and Cinzel ship as alternatives. Fonts ship unmodified; CI reads each face's name table and refuses to
subset a face that declares a Reserved Font Name; the OFL text ships in the notices file. Label metrics are read from
the bundled files (§9.2). The bundled faces are TrueType-flavoured (`glyf`), whose outlines SVG's default text writes
(§11.1); when the default face lacks `smcp`, the family's OFL small-caps cut is bundled unmodified beside it (§9.2); an
SVG export may embed a face unmodified as a data URI (§11.1). CI checks all three (§9.2).

### 17.3 Our own licence (D-22; DEF-14)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r1); drafted by fixall/draft-scope-r1

Until the owner chooses, the `plat/` repository is **proprietary: "Copyright © the owner. All rights reserved."** in its
`LICENSE` file, with no open-source licence. *Chose* this default *over* an open licence *because* it keeps every option:
the owner can later publish under any licence by one act, while an open licence once granted cannot be withdrawn from
those who received the code. Flagged for the owner's veto. What keeps every choice open: permissive-only dependencies
checked over the production closure (§17.4); nothing copyleft linked or bundled; the notices file; the clean-room chain
(§17.1); every file written by the program's seats for the owner, and no outside contribution without the owner's
written assent.

# PART II — STAGE 2: the city composed of neighbourhoods (interface depth; built after the base)

*In plain words.* Any district of the base town can be opened as a detailed neighbourhood — like watabou's
Neighbourhood generator — with blocks, plots, courtyards, hatched roofs, wells and local street names. The base
already draws every shared street, wall and shore exactly once, so two neighbourhoods never disagree about their
common edge; each district has its own random stream, so re-rolling one neighbourhood never touches another; and the
neighbourhood's look is just a closer level of detail of the same picture. Neighbourhood's four templates (area,
street, square, ring) become layout strategies the base can select per district, so a ring neighbourhood is laid by the
same engine that laid its neighbours.

## II.1 The district → neighbourhood interface

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r4; drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r4; earlier revisions fixall/integrate-r3, fixall/draft-pipeline-r3

```ts
interface Seam {                               // one per boundary run, created by S6 and read by both districts it separates — from milestone 1 (G-P1; NF-P6)
  id: Id; sides: [Id, Id | null];              // the two districts in address order; null: a one-sided run (frame, water, cliff, sky)
  edges: SeamEdge[];                           // in the first side's ring order; each: { chain: ChainRef /* the shared way, shore, wall, reservation-boundary or perimeter chain */, type: 'way'|'water'|'wall'|'reserve'|'field'|'cliff'|'frame'|'sky', reservation?: Id /* 'reserve' only: the reservation whose `reserved` boundary the run follows */, wayClass?, widthCm?, frontageSide?, hard: boolean }
  portals: Portal[];                           // every way that crosses or meets the run: { id, wayId, class, widthCm, at: VertexRef /* ('portal', id) */, bearing, from: 'growth'|'baseLane'|'closeup', by?: Id /* the district whose lane or close-up added it */ } — every one must be connected
  amendments: SeamAmendment[];                 // the vertices inserted on a shared spine after S6: S8's lane ends and close-up T-junctions — one record, so both sides always agree
  boundarySamples: { prosperity: Sample[]; density: Sample[]; greenery: Sample[]; terrain: Sample[] };   // along the run; `hard` seams jump, soft seams interpolate
}
interface SeamAmendment { kind: 'baseLane'|'tJunction'; spine: Id /* the shared boundary way */; vertex: VertexRef /* ('junction', the new junction's id): inserted at level 1 by splitThrough or as a lane's end */; portal: Id; by: Id /* the district whose batch inserted it */; cause: 'generation' | EditId /* S8's run, a regenerate, or the close-up's event */ }
interface SeamContract {                       // a district's view, assembled on demand from its Seam records; never stored
  district: Id; seams: Id[] /* in ring order */; sharedGeometry: 'ownedByBase';   // shared edges are generated once by the base; neighbourhoods change them only through a SeamAmendment
  plotLinesOnBoundary: EdgeSetRef[]; alleysOnBoundary: Id[];   // resolved from the district's own plots and alleys
  interiorSamples: { prosperity: Sample[]; density: Sample[]; greenery: Sample[]; terrain: Sample[] };   // on an interior lattice
}
interface NeighbourhoodRequest {
  district: Id; key: PlatKey /* the ground, or the sky island's arena */; boundary: TypedBoundary; seam: SeamContract; context: DistrictContext /* kind, venue mix, character, prosperity band, growth stage, water, walls, slope */;
  laid: { blocks: Id[]; plots: Id[]; alleys: Id[] };   // the base's own L2/L3 fabric under this district (R's `laid`)
  layer: 'ground' | 'sky';                     // sky: no portals, no roads in or out (the floating-island context); own terrain optional
  mode: 'refine' | 'replace';                  // refine: presentation detail only (derived); replace: a template fabric (a model edit, II.4)
  strategy: FabricStrategyId; params: Record<string, number>;   // 'bent-cut' (refine) | 'ring' | 'square' | 'street' (replace)
  outlineTemplate?: 'disc'|'d_shape'|'lozenge'|'crescent'|'spindle';   // standalone and sky calls only (§4.2 S1 (2))
  // streams: keyed from the district's lineage on demand (§6.1); nothing stored
  lod: 'neighbourhood';
}
interface NeighbourhoodResult { blocks: Block[]; ways: Way[]; plots: Plot[]; buildings: Building[]; greens: Greenery[]; pins: Pin[]; labels: LabelEntity[] /* §9.1 */; seams: SeamReport; report: StageReport }
interface SeamReport {                         // written by every close-up; its numbers are the S1 acceptance (II.5)
  portalsTotal: number; portalsConnected: number /* must equal portalsTotal */; unconnected: Id[]; addedPortals: SeamAmendment[];
  sharedEdgeHausdorffCm: Cm /* must be 0: shared edges are read from the base; an amendment only inserts a vertex on them */;
  fieldJumps: { at: PointCm /* a sample position, not a vertex */; field: 'prosperity'|'density'|'greenery'; delta: number; hard: boolean }[] /* a jump on a soft seam outside its band is a soft-invariant failure */;
  superseded: { old: Id; new: Id }[];          // §6.3's successions for the entities a template replacement re-derived (anchor rule, §2.1, §6.3)
}
interface NeighbourhoodStrategy { generate(req: NeighbourhoodRequest, ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<NeighbourhoodResult> }
// Pin is defined in §2.7 (the complete furniture vocabulary, in the entity registry from M1)
```

**Seam edge types (VK2-10).** An edge's type is the first its role rows give: `way` → `way`; `wall` → `wall`; `shore`
or `bank` → `water`, or `cliff` where the bank kind is cliff; `reserved` → `reserve`; `district_bound` alone (the
settlement perimeter) → `field`; `border` or `margin` → `frame`; a sky arena's outline → `sky`. A **`reserve`** run is a
reservation boundary two districts share with no way on it — a plaza's, precinct's or market's edge where the grower's
`validateEdge` stopped (§4.5): its shared geometry is the `reserved` chain and the two parts of the margin band that S10's
step (0) lays along it (§4.7); it has no portals; a close-up ends its plot lines on its own part's inner edge and writes
neither part (a `replace` close-up's scoped regeneration re-lays its own side's part, §7.3 item 2). `hard` comes from the
seam-type row of the editable tables (§7.6): `wall`, `water`, `cliff`, `frame` and `sky` hard; `way` and `field` soft;
`reserve` by the reservation's kind — castle and precinct hard; plaza, market, park and institution soft.

Rules: (1) the base generates every shared edge once and both districts read it; (2) a close-up either **refines** —
adds the neighbourhood-LOD presentation detail (roof construction and hatching, surfaces, pins, trees, local street
names) as a pure function of the district's committed base state, its sub-seed, strategy and params, never changing
L1–L4 geometry — or **replaces** the base's plots with a template layout inside its boundary with `ring` / `square` /
`street`; the templates are `FabricStrategy` registrations selected per district (G-P2), so a template district is laid
by the base's own engine with seams by construction; (3) **seam amendment (GEO-30):** a close-up may end a street on a
shared boundary spine (NG's cuts end on existing roads, 361 / 361; the ring template's radials run to the edge); each
such end is a T-junction inserted with `splitThrough` at level 1 so the shared spine stays one chain, recorded as a
`SeamAmendment` (kind `tJunction`) and a new portal in the shared `Seam` record that both districts' contracts read.
**The neighbour step (VK2-11)** is the only write on the other side, the same for a close-up's T-junction and for a lane
a district's reroll adds or removes on a shared spine (§4.6 step 7): one L2 batch whose only face is the neighbour's
half-corridor strip along the split spine edge inserts one `corridor_split` edge from the junction vertex to the foot of
its perpendicular on the neighbour's kerb — the edge `corridorUnion` builds on a side the spine passes straight through
(§3.7), so each spine sub-edge keeps its own strip (§2.2 rule 1) and that side gets no wedge. A half-corridor strip
holds no L3 content (avenue and street-tree rows are `Greenery.along` records, §2.7), so the batch clears nothing and
re-derives nothing: the neighbour's blocks, plots, footprints and greenery are neither in its face nor re-derived —
never its plots. The edge's kerb end lands, by §3.6's attraction, on a vertex of the kerb's route within `attractCm` — a
plot-line end or footprint corner there is promoted to L2 (§2.2 rule 3): every ring of the vertex's own level and finer
stays as it was, and each coarser ring along the kerb gains it — the neighbour's block at L2, and its plot at L3 when
the promoted vertex is an L4 footprint corner — each equal to its prior ring with the vertex removed (II.4's seam
exception; NP3-5) — and otherwise splits the kerb at L2 by the placement rule, which adds that one vertex to the rings
through it (each equal to its prior ring with the vertex removed; II.4's seam exception) and, by §2.6's wing-carrying
rule, to the wing ring of a building whose footprint fronts that stretch of kerb. Removing the street reverses the step,
whether by an undo, by the district's reroll or by any later edit: `removeEdges` takes the `corridor_split` out, the
strip is one face again, a kerb vertex the step created dissolves (`split` flag, no role) and leaves the wing ring it
joined, and a plot-line end or footprint corner the step promoted returns to its level by demotion — it kept its `split`
flag, which only a warp that has since moved it or the kerb vertices beside it clears, making the bend part of the
kerb's true shape (§3.6; VK4-3) — so the kerb's L2 route, index and digest, and every ring the step touched, are those
before the step, with any later change to the kerb kept (§2.2 rule 3; VK3-3, VK4-3). *Test (§13.1):* the step at a
plot-line end and at a footprint corner, each followed by the street's removal by a reroll, not an undo — the kerb's L2
route and digest, the block's and the plot's rings and the wing rings equal to those before the step. Every portal stays
connected (S1 acceptance: portal connection 100 %, shared-edge Hausdorff 0); (4) footprint hashes at city LOD and
neighbourhood LOD are identical for every entity a `refine` close-up covers (refinement never changes geometry); a
`refine` close-up is a derived refinement level outside the base digest until a `closeup` event is logged before its
first edit (§7.1, §7.4); a `replace` close-up re-derives its entities under the anchor rule and records §6.3's
successions in `SeamReport.superseded`; (5) the standalone no-portal mode is the same call with a synthetic boundary
drawn from an **outline template** (disc, D-shape, lozenge, crescent, spindle — NG's template outlines, our own shapes;
COV-NG-N06) through §4.2's closed-outline routine; the **sky-island call** is the same request with `layer: 'sky'`, an
outline from that routine, optional own terrain echoing the ground, no roads in or out, and a `reason` (II.6), its
shadow projected onto the ground layer by §8.4; (6) **base lanes on shared spines (NF-P6):** the lanes the base's own S8
ends on a district-boundary spine are the same kind of vertex, recorded in the same `Seam` record with kind `baseLane`
and kept at least a portal gap from every other portal on the spine (§4.6), so a close-up reads them like any portal and
a reroll of either district changes only the seam records it is party to, the vertices it inserts or removes and their
neighbour steps (3) (II.4). *Judgment (J-P33):* chose one `Seam` record per boundary run, read by both districts, over a
contract copied into each district, because one record cannot disagree with itself and a district's re-derivation then
changes the seams it is party to rather than its neighbour's district record. *Judgment (J-P37; VK2-10):* chose a
`reserve` seam type over forbidding two districts to meet along a reservation boundary without a way, because the
grower's `validateEdge` stops at reservation boundaries by design, so a plaza's or precinct's edge is exactly where
districts meet, and the margin band S10 already lays there is the shared geometry the type names. *Judgment (J-P38;
VK2-11):* chose one `corridor_split` insertion into the neighbour's half-corridor strip over re-running `corridorUnion`
on the neighbour's whole L1 face, because `corridorUnion` re-derives that face's built blocks and §3.3 keeps only the
content of stages before the one re-derived, so it would clear and re-derive every plot of the face, while the strip
holds no finer content and the one edge gives the same structure a from-scratch S9 builds at that vertex.

## II.2 Templates as fabric strategies (NG B2, B7, B8)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); earlier revision fixall/integrate-r1; drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r1

`RingFabric` (COV-NG-N12): concentric `secondary` ring roads inside the boundary at a radius law (a table) are the
template's only seed geometry — no template radials. The bands are processed **outside-in**, one hole-aware bent-cut
recursion per annulus (§4.6's slit, σ = 0.098): the band's **first cut is a slit** that opens the annulus without
splitting it, and the band's later cuts are its radial streets, arriving at the ring roads at right angles by the
recipe's perpendicular departure and arrival; because each band draws its cuts from its own sub-stream, radials are
**staggered band to band**, never one straight line through all rings (NG RA-2, RA-4, PF-1). Radials of the outermost
band that reach the boundary use the seam amendment of II.1 rule (3). `SquareFabric`: `mode: 'carved'` places a
rectangular or round plaza face at the district's centroid or at a portal, sized from population, frontages typed
`square`, then the bent cut on the remainder; `mode: 'void'` (COV-VG-VN-179) carves nothing — the plots whose frontages
face a chosen open area are left unbuilt, so the square is the irregular void their omission forms (NG 1.1.0's square,
IMPR S4's "keep NG's square as a void"); in both modes a centrepiece pin (monument, statue or fountain; COV-NG-XB23)
sits at the square's nexus. The `square` template row's default is `mode: 'void'` — NG's own square, which IMPR S4 keeps
— so a district opened with `square` and no mode, and every `square` pair of the D-5 panel against NG (§13.6 (2)), gets
the void; `carved` is the row's other value. A district records a non-default mode as `fabricParams.squareMode = 1`
(`carved`; 0 or absent is `void`), since `fabricParams` holds numbers (§2.5), set by `setAttr` like any fabric parameter
(II.4) (J-S42; VS4-4). `StreetFabric`: a main street between two portals with plots directly on it, bent cuts on the
deeper faces. **Template road widths (COV-NG-N20):** ring roads and template streets take fixed per-district widths
drawn once from the district's stream (NG: per-seed values), while cut streets follow §4.6's width law. A template is its seed geometry plus the number of sub-areas it hands to the bisector (CA-2 via the parity judge) and is a data row plus a
strategy class; the `area` template is the base's default. Templates chosen by context (S4) read the district context (a
quay district gets a quay-parallel street; an intramural district a ring near the wall; a stepped street on a slope).

## II.3 Block content dispatch, pins, local identities (S2 context features)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r1); drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r1

A stage-2 table maps `(block area, spacing to the nearest green, spacing to the nearest landmark or manor block, district
kind, prosperity band)` → the weighted choice NG makes among Normal / Manor / Empty / Green (CONFIDENCE B6: NG's
`createGreen` on 23–58 % of Normal blocks with no target is the failure — ours has a target per band, from §4.9's rules);
a **minimum landmark spacing** row keeps landmark and manor blocks apart (NG's "kept apart from each other"; COV-NG-XA07).
**Pins** of the neighbourhood tier (wells, fountains, large trees, statues, monuments, bandstands) are placed in yards and
squares by a probability gate per kind and band, as refine-mode presentation detail; the base's own pins (§4.7 S11) are
model entities and appear at every LOD. **Local street identities** (names, surfaces, widths) come from the way records and
the naming grammar; context features (quays, intervallum along the wall, stepped streets, bridge approaches) are constraints
available inside the boundary. A manor compound's enclosure wall and gate are the base's `PlotBound` treatments
(§2.5, §4.7 S11), so the close-up draws NG's walled compound from model data (COV-NG-N27).

## II.4 The render tier, the workflow and the close-up's persistence status (S5, S6)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r5); drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r5; earlier revisions fixall/integrate-r3, fixall/draft-pipeline-r3

The `hatched` preset at neighbourhood LOD (§8.2, §8.6): tapered hatch triangles from the ridge, two-tone roofs by the
measured law over the stored wings, prism shadows from stored heights, cobbles / tiles / outlined / dashed road programs,
chimneys, wells, lobed depth-sorted trees, the hood title in the emptiest corner; ≈ 25 canvas ops per wing as the
ceiling; instanced hatching.

**Persistence status (LC-18).** A `refine` close-up is **derived data**: a pure function of the district's committed base
state, sub-seed, strategy and params, identical whether computed eagerly or lazily, held outside the base hash and never
stored — so the town is the same before and after anyone opens a district. The first edit inside a close-up is preceded
by a logged `closeup` event (strategy and params, §7.1), from which point the close-up enters the digest under
`closeups` (§2.9) and replays exactly. Editing a close-up element (moving a well, removing a tree, restyling a pin) records
an **instance-override event** on the element's host entity and ordinal (§7.1),
which persists, undoes and replays after regeneration, re-matched by position; when the base re-derives the district, the
close-up re-derives with those overrides carried over and orphans reported. Close-up lanes, plots and houses are base
entities (the base's S8–S11 already produce the finest model fabric), so renaming a lane or locking a house is an ordinary
base edit. A `replace` close-up (a template fabric) is **a model edit**: `setAttr(district.fabric, template)` plus a scoped
regeneration of the district — logged, hashed, the same for every viewer, and visible at city LOD because city-LOD footprints
read the same model at every zoom.

**Workflow.** Open any district at neighbourhood LOD from the city view; "Same kind, new seed" per district with locks — New
random on the district, one of §7.1's named actions scoped to it; per-district reroll isolation — rerolling district D
leaves every other district byte-identical (R8) except the **seam exception** of §4.6 (NF-P6): the chains and `Corridor`
records of the ways that bound D; the half-corridor strips on both sides and the junction wedges at the vertices D's
batches insert or remove on those spines — S8's `baseLane` ends and a close-up's T-junctions — which on a neighbour's
side are only II.1 (3)'s neighbour step: one `corridor_split` edge and the one kerb vertex it lands on (promoted) or
adds; the neighbouring cells, plots and footprints whose rings pass through those vertices, and the wing rings of the
buildings on them (§2.6's wing-carrying rule), which change only by them — the same polygon point for point, checked
by comparing the rings with the vertices removed, and a promoted vertex returning to its level when the lane goes
(§2.2 rule 3; NP4-1) — and the `Seam` records D is party to. This is the set §4.6 step 7 and §7.3 item 1 state, and
the one II.5's reroll-isolation tests check. The locality oracle
computes this set from the batches' commit records and checks everything else byte for byte (§7.3). Export of one
district as its own SVG / PNG / VTT scene.

## II.5 What the base already carries for stage 2 (all base requirements in PART I)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r3); drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r3

Typed boundary edges with `hard` flags and portals in the shared `Seam` records of every district (§2.5, II.1), the lane
ends S8 puts on boundary spines included (§4.6); shared geometry owned by the base (§2.2) with the
seam-amendment protocol and `splitThrough` (§3.4, II.1); plot lines and alleys on the boundary (§4.7); seam-continuous
prosperity, density and greenery fields with hard / soft seams (§4.5); per-district streams keyed from each district's
lineage (§6.1); the hole-aware bent cut
with the measured recipe (§4.6); the `FabricStrategy` slot (§14, G-P2) with `BentCutFabric` registered from M1 and the three
template fabrics registered at M5; stored wings, boundary treatments and the complete pin vocabulary (§2.5–§2.7); the
neighbourhood LOD band declared in the display list and the `hatched` programs (§8); the world-aligned tile pyramid (§8.8),
invalidated by per-district dirty regions; the
per-district regeneration budget ≤ 30 ms (§12); the close-up persistence rule and the instance-override event (II.4, §7.1);
the sky context and outline templates (§2.1, §4.2, II.6). Acceptance for stage-2 readiness of the base itself, before any
close-up generator exists (M1 exit): on every B-CITY city every district's `SeamContract` view resolves completely — every
boundary run belongs to exactly one `Seam` record, every seam edge carries one of II.1's types (a way-less reservation
boundary between two districts as `reserve`, with its two margin-band parts), every portal's vertex resolves, and
every `baseLane` portal matches
exactly one S8 lane end and every lane end on a boundary spine one `baseLane` portal — 100 %; and a New random on each of
20 districts per city changes nothing outside its seam exception (II.4). Acceptance for stage 2 itself (M5 exit, §16), read from the `SeamReport` of II.1: portals connected 100 % (added
portals included); shared-edge Hausdorff distance 0; field jumps on soft seams within band; the footprint hash at
neighbourhood LOD identical to the city-LOD hash for every entity a refine close-up covers; opening a district ≤ NG's
recorded 10–96 ms at comparable counts and per-district regeneration ≤ 30 ms (§12); rerolling one district leaves every
other district byte-identical outside the seam exception of II.4; the model hash unchanged by opening, closing or reopening any
number of districts.

## II.6 The staged layers — floating islands and sewers: the hooks the base carries now

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r2); drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r2

*In plain words.* The owner stages both layers as toggles after the city is mastered. Nothing here is built in the base,
but every record and interface they need exists now, so adding them later is a registration, not a redesign.

**Floating islands (AM-2; DEF-7).** The toggle creates 1–3 islands. **Why an island exists** is one of two reasons, by rule or
by assignment: `prosperity` — the island carries a very prosperous neighbourhood or set of neighbourhoods; by rule, when the
toggle is on, the roster's richest demand for up to three districts' worth of households is allocated by S7b to sky
pseudo-districts instead of the ground (so the population stays whole) — S7b creates each sky pseudo-district's
`Allocation` itself, first and before any island exists: its plot land is the island's area, drawn from
`IslandRule.areaHaBand` on the `island.place` stream, × the dense core's plot share, filled from the richest band down at
each band's plot area (§4.5 S7b (5); NF-P13); `institution` — the island carries one unique
institution chosen from an `IslandInstitution` row (a palace overlooking the land, a cathedral, a prison isolating
criminals) or named by an assignment. **What it is:** a `SkyIsland` (§2.7) with an organic oval outline from §4.2's
routine (the `disc` or `lozenge` outline template), an elevation from a band row, and optionally its own terrain from S1 run
on the sky plat with an *echo* request — its relief `echo` or `own`, and a conjured river that takes the ground river's
bearing and width law; its districts are laid by the ordinary pipeline through a `NeighbourhoodRequest` with `layer: 'sky'`
(no portals, no roads in or out). **Where it floats:** a placement rule reads the ground plan — over water, fields or
outskirts by default, over the core only by assignment; the occlusion mode (opaque, ghost the covered ground, offset view) is
a rendering choice (§8.4). **What it does not do:** it has no relation to the underground layer; its shadow falls on the
ground through the shadow pass; it exports as its own layer (§11). Hook interface:

```ts
interface IslandRule { reason: 'prosperity'|'institution'; maxIslands: 1|2|3; elevationCmBand: [Cm, Cm]; areaHaBand: [number, number]; placement: ('water'|'fields'|'outskirts')[]; terrain: 'none'|'echo'|'own' }
interface SkyStrategy { place(doc: Document, rules: IslandRule[], allocations: Allocation[] /* S7b's sky pseudo-district allocations */, ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<SkyIsland[]> }
// a Stage registered after S7b by declared I/O: inputs S7b's sky allocations and the ground plan; outputs the islands (outline sized to each
// allocation's area, placement by rule), their arenas and their districts, which run the ordinary pipeline through a NeighbourhoodRequest
```

**Sewers (DEF-7).** A `SewerStrategy` registers as a stage after S11 (declared inputs: ways with `flowToward`, the drainage
raster and outfalls of §2.3, plots and buildings with their class table's `drain` column, the underground plat; output:
`Tunnel` records, §2.7). Its rule families are data: `follow-streets` (mains under the ways, falling with `flowToward` to the
outfalls), `drainage-lines` (along the natural drainage), `mixed`; which buildings need drains is the class table's column;
two presets — `historical` (restrained: open gutters, a few culverted mains, cess pits by class) and `navigable` (the fantasy
preset: large vaulted mains with chambers). It renders through the ground by §8.4's cut-away or overlay and exports as the
underground layer.

```ts
interface SewerStrategy { derive(doc: Document, rules: { family: 'follow-streets'|'drainage-lines'|'mixed'; preset: 'historical'|'navigable' }, ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<Tunnel[]> }
```

# PART III — What a later village product needs from the base (one page; the hooks are concrete)

> PENDING FABLE REVIEW — revised by opus stand-in (fixall/integrate-r2); drafted by fixall/draft-pipeline-r2

*In plain words.* The village generator is a separate product the owner stages after the town, with its own ladder
(thorp → hamlet → village). This page lists what it would take from the base, the hooks the base carries for it now, and
confirms nothing here stands in its way; the base does not pay for it.

**What it would reuse unchanged:** the kernel and plat (§2–§3); the site model — descent-traced rivers with a carved field,
level-set ponds, the coast routine (§4.2) — and, for VG's own order, a `RiverStrategy` that lays a terrain-independent
spline course first (VG's live course runs through 6–7 control points before its terrain; COV-VG-WC2) and asks S1 to carve
the field to it, which S1's carve step already does; the sequential roster and lazy people (§10); the frontage-first plot
machinery and the site-plan tables, which already contain cottage, farmstead and detached-in-yard classes (§4.7); the
hinterland presets incl. the VG sector look, orchards and commons (§4.9); the `palisade` enceinte kind (§2.7); the display
list, style sheets, the base's relief tier (hillshade, contour and hachure marks, §8.2) and the reserved `painterly` preset
slot (§8.2); the document, edits, exports and the API (§7, §11).

**What it would add behind hooks the base now carries (DEF-15):**
1. **A density stage before its network (COV-VG-VN-002).** The pipeline is the topological order of declared stage I/O
   (§4.1, §4.12), so a `VillageStrategy` registers a density `StageDecl` whose output the network stage declares as an
   input; VG computes its density before its roads, and the base's S6 order does not bind it.
2. **A palisade before its roads (MN-4, COV-VG-VN-003).** On the live VG build 19365073 the palisade is built before the roads
   — the hull of the populated points of a 10 × 10 lattice over the density field, cleaned and smoothed — and the road
   trackers consult it at every step, gates falling where they meet it (`profile-village.md` New-build addendum N2, P1).
   The village registers an `EnceinteStrategy` that builds exactly that from its density stage, and its tracker-steered
   `NetworkStrategy` receives the result through the `enceintes` input every network strategy now takes (§4.12).
3. **A tracker-steered network** (VG's roads are steered trackers, not A\* — `_critic-vg-ng.md`) with one through-road and
   partial driveways, and a **"houses along ways" `FabricStrategy`** with no block cutting.
4. **One district (COV-VG-WC4).** A village is modelled as **one district** of kind `village` (one quarter) covering the
   settlement; its blocks are the large faces between ways and its plots line the ways, so the containment invariant
   building ⊂ plot ⊂ block ⊂ district holds unchanged and nothing in §2–§4 needs a village exception.
5. **A size ladder below TOWN.** Rung rows THORP ≈ 20–80, HAMLET ≈ 80–400, VILLAGE ≈ 400 up to (not including) 1 500
   inhabitants (our own rows, calibratable; VG spans ≈ 130–1 700); a request of 1 500 or more is a base TOWN (§1.1, D-33)
   whose size follows its population within its rung, and below 1 500 `LadderRouter` routes to the village product; a
   village request's default is not a walled circle (walls are a rule keyed on rung); VG's independent tree stream is a
   keyed sub-stream (already the design); VG's spotlight vignette and grass-tuft look as `painterly` programs — the hillshade,
   contour and hachure marks are already the base's relief tier (§8.2), built at M2b (§16), so the village adds none of
   them (COV-VG-VN-029).

**Not-precluded checks** (the parity judge's 44 / 44): the strategy registry admits every strategy above; the level model
tolerates nearly empty L2 / L3; model time is near-linear in building count; every VG rendering row has a program or a
preset slot; terrain-and-water-as-one-picture is the base's own model. **What the base does not pay for:** tracker
steering, the palisade construction, VG's spotlight and painterly look, the palisade look, VG's grammar and its tag
vocabulary.
